items.title: PVR Inox shares jump 6% in 2 days, hit fresh 52-week high as CRISIL upgrades outlook to positive. What is it seeing
items.summary: Shares of PVR Inox jumped around 4% on Wednesday, extending gains to over 6% in two days after ratings agency CRISIL revised its outlook for the firm’s long-term bank facilities and non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to ‘Positive’ from ‘Stable’.PVR Inox shares hit a fresh 52-week high of around Rs 1,740 apiece on NSE today, pushing its market capitalisation above Rs 17,060 crore. Along with the outlook upgrade, CRISIL Ratings also reaffirmed its 'Crisil AA' rating on the long term debt instruments of the company.Why did Crisil upgrade its outlook for PVR Inox?The rating on the short-term bank facilities and commercial paper programme has been reaffirmed at 'Crisil A1+'. The ratings agency said the outlook upgrade was driven by expectations of sustained growth in the company’s scale of operations across multiple revenue streams and improvement in operating margin strengthening its business risk profile. The outlook revision also accounts for the strengthening of the company’s financial risk profile by becoming a net cash company during the first half of fiscal 2027.Also read | District's PVR INOX ticket sales jump 60%, rivals lag at 4%The structural improvement is driven by PVR Inox’s ability to monetise its network more consistently across content cycles, thereby reducing content concentration risk, Crisil said. It added that the content ecosystem has become increasingly diversified, with admissions being supported by a broader mix of Hindi, regional and Hollywood content. The industry has also witnessed increasing success of mid-budget films which lowers the dependence on a few marquee releases and provides greater stability to admissions and occupancy.Alternate content initiatives such as re-releases, concert screenings, anime content and sports broadcasts have also emerged as supplementary demand drivers and improve utilisation of the existing screen network, Crisil said. It noted that the concerns around OTT-led disruption have also moderated as the theatrical-first release model has been re-established, with producers increasingly using theatrical performance as the primary benchmark for content monetisation on OTT, highlighting the complementary nature of theatrical and digital channels.PVR Inox’s business risk profile is also supported by increasing geographical diversification as the company continues to expand its presence in southern India and tier 2 and 3 markets, which benefit from strong movie-going culture, multiple thriving film industries and relatively low multiplex penetration, the ratings agency said, further noting that the company’s screen portfolio in southern markets increased from 31% at the end of fiscal 2023 to 34% in at the end of first half of fiscal 2027, with more than 35% of screen additions over the past three years originating from the region. “This diversification supports admissions visibility and reduces dependence on any single language or regional content cycle,” it said.Crisil further highlighted PVR Inox’s earnings, pointing out that the company demonstrated healthy revenue growth driven by a mix of increasing admissions, increasing average ticket prices (ATP), higher spends per head (SPH), and improving monetisation of its customer base. Net debt reduced, aided by strong accrual generation and proceeds from the divestment of the 4700 BC business for about Rs 227 crore in January 2026. Despite completion of a Rs 300 crore maiden share buyback in the first half of fiscal 2027, leverage metrics are expected to remain comfortable, the ratings agency said. It expects the company’s net worth to remain healthy and gradually improve over the medium term, supported by strong accrual.“The ratings reflect the company’s strong market position with an established brand, expectation of further improvement in operating efficiency, led by synergistic benefits and premiumisation, and a strong financial risk profile. These strengths are partially offset by inherent volatility of the film exhibition business with operating performance remaining dependent on the quality and timing of content releases and evolving consumer preferences,” it said.Also read | PVR INOX bets on smaller multiplexes as single-screens declinePVR Inox share pricePVR Inox shares jumped more than 9% in a week and 23% in a month. This comes amid blockbuster releases including Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Part 1. The stock has so far gained more than 70% in 2026.The shares of the multiplex chain operator have delivered 55% returns over one year. In the longer term, the stock gained more than 4.5% in three years and 2% in five years. items.title: Cambridge Dictionary chooses 'human' as word of the year amid AI fears
items.summary:
Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge Dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026 cultural zeitgeist.
"Human," the dictionary's word of the year, is not just a throwback but also a backlash of sorts that reflects the debate over how AI has blurred the lines between machines and people.
"AI is changing how we talk about being human," said Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer. "Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children."
The adjective derived from the Latin "humanus" and in use since the 1450s is defined by Cambridge as "having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines."

items.summary: Shares of ACME Solar rallied up to 3% on Thursday, hitting an intraday high of Rs 416 on the NSE. The gains came after the company, through its subsidiary ACME Alpha Renewable, signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with NTPC for a 150 MW Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS)-connected hybrid power project at a tariff of Rs 3.21 per unit under NTPC’s Hybrid-IV tranche. According to a filing with the exchange, the company said that the tariff for this project has already been adopted by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC). The order has been awarded by NTPC, with the scheduled commencement of power supply set for June 30, 2028. The project will have a tenure of 25 years from the scheduled commencement date.Also Read | Nvidia shares jump 5% in after hours as quarterly earnings beat estimates. Is the storm around Huang’s exit finally over?The hybrid project, spanning Bhadla in Rajasthan, Jambkhabalia in Gujarat and Mandsaur in Madhya Pradesh, will combine solar and wind energy with suitable energy storage solutions.It is designed to provide reliable and dispatchable power throughout the day while meeting offtakers' requirements during peak demand hours. CTU transmission connectivity has been secured for the Jambkhabalia and Mandsaur locations.The project marks an important step towards ACME Solar's goal of contributing to India's clean energy transition. Following the signing of this PPA, the company's under-construction, PPA-backed portfolio stands at 5,080 MW, out of a total under-construction contracted capacity of 5,380 MW.“This PPA with NTPC reinforces our focus on delivering reliable renewable power aligned with the evolving needs of India’s energy market. By combining solar, wind and energy storage, the project will help meet peak-hour demand and support India’s clean energy transition,” said Nikhil Dhingra, Joint MD and CEO of ACME Solar.The company also clarified that neither its promoters, promoter group nor group companies have any interest in the entity that awarded the contract. It added that the order does not fall under related-party transactions.On November 16, the company announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, ACME Greentech Sixteen, had signed a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with Rewa Ultra Mega Solar to set up a 220 MW solar project with a Battery Energy Storage System at Morena Solar Park in Madhya Pradesh.The project has a scheduled commercial operation date of December 31, 2027, and a tariff of Rs 2.764 per unit.Also Read | IIFL Finance shares jump 5% after 13% stake changes hands in block deal, Fairfax likely sellerACME Solar share priceACME Solar shares have gained around 0.68% over the past month and 73.56% so far this calendar year. The Federal Aviation Administration has paused the installation of the routers that were linked to last week's national ground stop, and turned off any Juniper routers that were already installed.
The decision was made after technicians linked Friday's disruption of key air traffic control systems to one of these routers that had just been installed in El Dorado, Arkansas.
For now, the FAA is relying on older Cisco routers that have been in place for 25 years to continue operating the network while they investigate the cause of Friday's problems at 17 of the nation's 22 regional air traffic control centers.
The routers that malfunctioned last week are being tested in a lab at the headquarters of the company that installed them named L3Harris.

items.title: US judge blocks Trump curbs on student work
items.summary: A federal judge on Tuesday blocked President Donald Trump's administration from restricting the types of internships and other practical training opportunities available to international students attending US universities on visas.US District Judge Julia Kobick in Boston issued an injunction barring the US Department of Homeland Security from enforcing two August directives that higher education groups said had abruptly disrupted training opportunities for foreign students nationwide.Kobick, an appointee of former Democratic President Joe Biden, ruled in a lawsuit filed last month by four organizations, including the Association of American Universities and the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration.It marked the latest victory for plaintiffs challenging efforts by the Trump administration to impose restrictions on student visa holders as part of its hardline immigration agenda. On Monday, a different federal judge in Boston struck down a new rule that would limit how long ‌foreign students can remain in the US without applying for extensions.DHS declined to comment.The education groups in the case before Kobick argued that DHS had sharply narrowed rules that for more than 35 years governed international students' participation in internships and other practical training through a program known as curricular practical training, or CPT.They said foreign students historically could take part in school-authorized internships and training opportunities as long as they were directly related to their field of study and formed an integral part of an established curriculum.According to the plaintiffs, the government long interpreted that standard to allow participation when training either carried academic credit or was required to earn a degree.Amazon and Tesla were the top two employers of CPT students in 2024, when 140,775 student visa holders were authorized to participate in CPT overall, according to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.But in August, DHS, which oversees ICE, issued messages telling universities that internships and other opportunities qualified only if they were mandatory for every student in a degree program and did not cover elective training taken for academic credit.The agency said it had seen an increase in CPT authorizations it believed did not comply with program requirements and would increase scrutiny of approvals.Kobick found the directives were likely arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act as DHS had failed to acknowledge that it was making a "fundamental" change to the government's longstanding interpretation of the program's rules."Correct or not, this new interpretation is inconsistent with the government's previous position," she wrote.

Delhi records Nov's cleanest air at AQI 204, but relief may be short-lived
items.summary:
Delhi recorded its cleanest air this month on Tuesday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) settling at 204 in the 'poor' category, offering some respite after days of deteriorating air quality, though the relief is likely to be short-lived.
The last time the national capital recorded a lower AQI was on October 31, when the index stood at 117 in the 'moderate' category. Tuesday's reading was the lowest recorded in November, making it the least polluted day of the month so far.
The relatively better air quality on Tuesday was partly due to favourable meteorological conditions, the Air Quality Early Warning System said.
Northwesterly winds reaching speeds of up to 15 kmph and a mixing depth of around 1,500 metres helped disperse pollutants.

items.title: Nvidia shares crash 24% amid Huang scandal. Why UBS sees 54% upside
items.summary: Shares of Nvidia have plunged around 24% since the start of the month, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market value amid controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's alleged extramarital affair with a Chinese spy and his subsequent resignation. However, UBS has sought to allay investor concerns, pointing to attractive valuations following the sharp selloff.While many analysts are sounding the alarm over Nvidia’s future, UBS thinks the assumptions are brutal and unlikely to be correct, given the chip giant's momentum for at least two more years, even without Huang as CEO, Yahoo Finance reported. In essence, the market assumes that 2028 will be the peak for Nvidia, with no growth thereafter and EBITDA margins compressing by 1,500 basis points, UBS analyst Tim Arcuri wrote on Monday. "This seems incredibly draconian to us."Nvidia valuations after selloffThe UBS analyst believes that the near-term damage to the stock has been done. He believes that it doesn't make sense to give up on the stock after being down this much especially ahead of January hyperscaler earnings calls where the international brokerage thinks capex will be guided higher than current Street expectations.UBS maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Nvidia shares but reduced its target price to $240 apiece from $300 per share. The latest target price still implies around 54% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of $156.14 apiece.Also read | Nvidia board not considering Jensen Huang's return as CEO, focuses on probe: ReportBank of America analyst Vivek Arya, as quoted by the report, also feels that the stock has become sharply cheap after the selloff. He noted that 11x forward PE is a multi-decade low and a 36% forward discount to close peer Broadcom, reflecting a considerable amount of stress and potential for rebound.All eyes on Nvidia earningsNvidia is all set to announce its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, with investors eagerly awaiting the chipmaker’s results after Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy and his subsequent resignation sparked a massive 24% plunge in the stock this month so far.The Q3 earnings print would mark the first quarterly results announcement without Huang at the helm of the chipmaker. He resigned as the CEO of the company last week, following which Nvidia's finance chief, Colette Kress, took charge as the interim CEO. Its board has said it is in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role.Nvidia’s earnings also come at a critical juncture in the AI trade. Earlier this year, chip linked stocks rallied sharply as hyperscalers spiked their AI spendings and new innovations related to the nascent technology came to light. However, analysts soon began to question the massive capex plans and whether they will actually bear fruits in future, leading to an equally sharp downturn in the stocks that rallied during the frenzy.Nvidia is seen as one of the faces of the artificial intelligence-led boom. Its earnings will likely be taken by the market as one of the key metrics for where the AI trade stands, setting the trajectory for the overall sector.Also read | Nvidia Earnings Preview: 6 key factors investors will watchDisclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Fed's Barr flags AI risks to financial stability, warns of market disruption
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr has warned that artificial intelligence could pose growing risks to financial markets, cybersecurity and consumer protection, raising concerns about the technology's potential to destabilise the financial system, according to a report by Reuters.Barr's remarks follow the US Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report, released on Friday, which showed that 87% of surveyed contacts identified AI as a significant risk to the financial system. Concerns included AI-powered cyberattacks, complex financing arrangements and the possibility of a slowdown in AI-related earnings triggering a broader stock market decline.Also Read |South Korean stocks fall for fourth day as AI worries hit chipmakersAccording to Reuters, Barr on Monday highlighted additional risks, including the possibility that widespread reliance on AI-driven trading models could encourage herd behaviour and amplify market volatility. He also warned that self-learning algorithms could potentially manipulate markets and create financial instability.Barr raised concerns about the growing use of AI agents in retail banking, noting that banks could struggle to establish whether an AI system attempting to access or operate customer accounts has received proper authorisation. Even legitimate AI agents acting on behalf of customers could accelerate bank runs by moving money at unprecedented speeds, potentially overwhelming traditional safeguards, the report stated.Also Read |Chinese yuan steadies near two-week peak ahead of Xi-Trump meetingCybersecurity presents another significant challenge, with AI-enabled attackers and rogue AI agents potentially exploiting vulnerabilities across the financial system, Barr said.He also cautioned that AI developers face challenges in ensuring their models are properly controlled, legally precise, explainable and reproducible. The technology could reinforce existing biases in consumer lending and create risks of collusion, market manipulation and trading strategies capable of triggering significant volatility or systemic instability.Barr's comments, prepared for delivery in Milan, Italy, came ahead of a conference at the San Francisco Federal Reserve, where Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was scheduled to bring together AI developers, business leaders and academics to discuss the technology's implications for productivity, employment and the broader economy.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: FirstCry shares rally 13% to one-month high. Why JM Financial sees 55% upside even after cutting target price
items.summary: Shares of FirstCry-operator Brainbees Solutions jumped around 13% on Tuesday, snapping a three-session losing streak and post Q2 earnings gloom. While JM Financial reduced target price, it sees sharp margin recovery in the ongoing third quarter of FY27.FirstCry shares jumped to nearly Rs 179 apiece on NSE on Tuesday, the highest level seen by the stock since mid October this year. The stock is on track to record the sharpest single day jump since March this year.FirstCry Q2 ResultsThe company this weekend reported 14% year-on-year (YoY) growth in operating revenue to Rs 2,396 crore in the September quarter of FY27. Its net loss narrowed by 75% YoY to Rs 12.6 crore during the quarter under review, from Rs 51 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.Also read | FirstCry Q2 revenue rises 14% to Rs 2,396 crore, net loss narrows 75%Following the Q2 earnings print, the shares of the company edged 1% lower on Monday, before rebounding massively today.JM Financial on FirstCry share priceJM Financial maintained its ‘Buy’ call on the shares of FirstCry but reduced its target price to Rs 245 apiece from Rs 255 apiece. The latest target price still implies a whopping 55% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 159 apiece on NSE.The domestic brokerage noted that the company reported a mixed Q2 earnings print with consolidated revenue growth of 14% YoY, led by continued recovery in India multi-channel (IMC) while margins remained under pressure. Further, gross margin pressures due to residual diaper discounting and crude-linked cost pressures led to EBITDA decline.International revenue grew 6% YoY amid geopolitical disruptions while profitability improved. GlobalBees revenue rose around 8% YoY, impacted by a warehouse transition and festive or platform sales shifting into Q3. With portfolio rationalisation and the transition now complete, the company’s management now expects stronger growth and margins from Q3 onwards.Consolidated gross margin declined 154 bps YoY to 35.1%. However, FirstCry’s management indicated that these headwinds are easing with diaper competition moderating and gross margins expected to recover sharply from Q3 FY27. Following the Q2 FY27 gross margin miss, JM Financial cut FY27 adjusted EBITDA estimates by 18%, while broadly maintaining FY28-29 estimates, as it believes that the worst is likely behind.Also read | Can Paytm shares finally rise above IPO price? Jefferies hikes target price, estimates after RBI's nod for wallet comebackFirstCry share priceFirstCry shares later pared some gains to trade around 9% higher at around Rs 173 apiece on the NSE. The stock has gained 7% in a week but dropped 3% in a month. Overall, the shares of the company have fallen 40% in 2026 so far.In the longer term, FirstCry shares have dropped 48% in one year. items.title: US court strikes down Trump's plan to cap foreign students' visa stays
items.summary:
A US federal court has struck down a Trump administration proposal to cap the amount of time foreign students, scholars, and journalists can spend in the country on their respective visas.
In July, the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval.
Boston federal Judge F Dennis Saylor delivered a ruling on Monday striking down the DHS proposal as "arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law."
"Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity - providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States - that Congress sought to permit and encourage," Judge Saylor said in his ruling.
"The statute simply does not grant DHS such broad and open-ended authority to undermine the F-1 visa programme," he added.

items.title: Net dollar purchases more than halve in October as hedging curbs support rupee
items.summary: Mumbai: Net dollar purchases in the forwards market more than halved through October from the previous month to about $17 billion as targeted regulatory curbs on hedging took effect, building stability in the value of the rupee that surged from the end of the month to anchor a stunning revival of overseas interest in India-listed growth assets.The Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR), brought in to dissuade unnecessary currency hedging amid a haemorrhage that even record hauls from forex-inflow programmes couldn't seemingly staunch, immediately reduced dollar purchases in the forward market in October to $49 billion from $76 billion in September, CCIL data showed.135906856Dollar sales, meanwhile, reduced to $32 billion from $41 billion, marking a broader reduction in dollar demand that stood in sharp relief against a steady climb in the dollar index over the past four weeks. The dollar climbed 1.5% against a basket of six heavily traded currencies through this period, while the removal of state oil retailers' demand from the spot market and absence of unnecessary hedging provided the spot rupee the cushion it needed to draw in overseas funds.Read more: Indian equities ride global AI trade unwind: Is D-Street back on foreign investors' radar? BNP Paribas answers"Overall hedging has gone down after FERR and things have got more stringent. So, hedging happens only for what is required," said Sajal Gupta, head of forex and commodities at Nuvama. "Importers are hedging on a short-term basis while exporters still feel that the weakness in the rupee may reappear and are holding back on hedging."Read more: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on TuesdayHedging demand over the last few years has contributed to increased dollar demand, with importers hedging more and exporters hedging less.The rupee has recovered since mid-October, after touching near 97 levels last month. It closed at 93.92 on Monday, and has gained more than 3% from its record low levels.'Weakness Bias'The gap between forward dollar purchases and sales widened to $233 billion in FY26 from $97 billion in FY24, indicating a substantial increase in net dollar demand arising from hedging activity. Importers increasingly hedged amid expectations of sustained rupee deprecation, while exporters reduced their dollar sales, thus increasing dollar demand.FERR increased importer hedging costs by requiring banks to park 20% of the rupee value of eligible forward contracts with the RBI in non-interest-bearing cash reserves. This raises banks' funding and opportunity costs, which are passed on to importers through higher hedging charges, making forward dollar purchases more expensive."However, the effectiveness of FERR will depend on how long importer hedging remains curtailed. If the expectation of continued rupee depreciation persists, then importer hedging could pick up," said Gaura Sengupta, chief economist, IDFC First Bank.

items.title: Gold price slides to one-year low, heads for worst year since 2015
items.summary: Gold fell to a one-year low on Monday as elevated Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy weighed on demand, putting bullion on course for its worst annual performance in more than a decade, Reuters reported.According to a Reuters analysis, prices dropped to $3,830.74 a troy ounce, their lowest level since October 2, 2025. Gold has fallen 31.5% since reaching a record $5,594.82 in January and is heading for its worst year since 2015.“Markets expect higher interest rates ahead, boosting the dollar and compounding gold’s headwinds, leaving it exposed to deeper declines,” Nikos Tzabouras, senior financial editorial writer at FXCM, told Reuters.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe dollar is trading near its highest level since April 2025, making dollar-denominated bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies and weakening demand in recent months.Treasury yields have also risen as markets price in a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, along with a smaller probability of a 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Volatility in Nvidia shares has added to the pressure. The chipmaker’s market value fell by $1.9 trillion from early October to $3.9 trillion as of Friday, potentially prompting investors to sell gold to raise cash.“In the short term gold is a liquidity asset … the thing you sell to raise cash,” Nicky Shiels at MKS PAMP told Reuters.Middle East war fuels inflation concernsThe US-Israeli war against Iran, which began in late February, has driven oil prices higher, adding to inflation and fueling expectations of tighter monetary policy worldwide.Although non-yielding gold is traditionally viewed as a hedge against inflation, it tends to lose appeal when interest rates rise because it does not generate income.Physically backed gold exchange-traded funds attracted 211 metric tons of inflows during the third quarter despite higher bond yields and a stronger dollar. Demand for bars and coins, however, declined sharply.Also Read: Morgan Stanley turns bullish on global stocks, targets S&P 500 at 8,700Central-bank demand may weakenCentral banks remained active buyers earlier in the year, purchasing an estimated 675 tons between January and September, according to the World Gold Council.Demand from this segment could slow after Poland, the year’s most active official buyer, reached its target of 700 tons of gold reserves in November. Its central-bank governor nevertheless left open the possibility of additional purchases.China remained a rare source of strength. Its central bank has purchased gold for two years, supporting domestic investment sentiment.Despite the selloff, gold has so far remained above the psychologically important level of $3,800 an ounce.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Dow sinks 700 pts, Nasdaq over 2% as Huang exit fuels tech rout ahead of Nvidia Q3 earnings
items.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Monday as Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO deepened the selloff in AI shares, putting greater focus on the chipmaker’s Tuesday earnings and Anthropic’s IPO later this week.The S&P 500 lost 143.26 points, or 1.89%, to end at 7,418.41 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 620.16 points, or 2.47%, to 24,516.11. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 721.40 points, or 1.38%, to 51,626.15.Losses accelerated through the session, pushing the S&P 500 and Dow down more than 1% each. The Nasdaq tumbled over 2%, weighed down by a 4.6% drop in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.For live updates on US Markets, click here“It’s the back-and-forth in this market of the AI-related stocks catching a bid versus this rotation trade,” Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville told Reuters. “Over the last couple of weeks, it’s like a day-to-day thing where, you know, some days the AI names absolutely rip and then the very next day, you know, they’re in a freefall.”“There are signs underneath the surface that investors aren’t panic-selling and running away from the asset class altogether, but are probing other corners of the equity market,” Mayfield added.Nvidia fell 4.2%, leading every member of the Magnificent Seven group of megacap technology stocks lower. Huang’s resignation following allegations of an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China added to existing concerns about AI’s rapid expansion and potential risks.Huang’s abrupt departure also prompted the Trump administration to announce new restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia. The move came ahead of US President Donald Trump’s expected meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.The selloff marks a sharp reversal for semiconductor stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had gained 106.6% for the year by mid-June, but its advance has since narrowed to about 43%. That is still roughly four times the S&P 500’s gain in 2026.Also Read | Michael Burry warns of 'mild manipulation' in Nvidia's China sales. What Big Short investor expects for the stockThe retreat has pushed the Nasdaq more than 10% below its record closing high from October 6, confirming that the index is in a correction.Nvidia is expected to report a 90.4% year-over-year increase in earnings on revenue of $109.10 billion.Warsh comments and rate outlookFederal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said Monday that technological advances could significantly affect the economy. Potential outcomes range from stronger growth with broadly shared gains to higher unemployment and an economic slowdown if expected investment returns fail to materialise.Investors are awaiting minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee’s latest meeting, due Wednesday, for clues about the policy path ahead of next month’s interest-rate decision.Markets see a 96% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Among individual stocks, chipmakers Intel and Micron declined sharply, alongside AI cloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius. Major cloud companies Alphabet, Amazon and Meta also ended substantially lower, while server makers Dell and Super Micro Computer posted steep losses.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Indian equities ride global AI trade unwind: Is D-Street back on foreign investors' radar? BNP Paribas answers
items.summary: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have returned to Indian equities with purchases worth nearly $8 billion over 15 trading sessions, as global investors reassess their exposure to AI-linked stocks, offering a fresh boost to Dalal Street after nearly two years of sustained foreign selling. Between October 21 and November 10, foreign investors bought approximately $8 billion worth of Indian equities, reversing around 16% of the nearly $50 billion they had sold over the preceding two years, according to a report by BNP Paribas.The renewed foreign buying has coincided with a strong recovery in domestic equities, with the benchmark Nifty50 gaining around 10% over the past one month."The return of foreign capital comes against the backdrop of significant selling in other Asian markets. FIIs sold $9 billion worth of equities in South Korea and $26 billion in Taiwan, while major regional indices came under pressure. Over the 30-day period cited in the report, the Nasdaq declined around 7%, South Korea's KOSPI fell 16% and Japan's Nikkei dropped 10%.ALSO READ: Coal India's 3rd big windfall in a year? How Mahanadi Coalfields IPO could unlock Rs 8,964 croreBNP Paribas said India was capturing a portion of the global portfolio rotation away from the AI theme. The investment bank attributed the shift to concerns over whether returns on capital would justify the substantial expenditure on AI infrastructure and the possibility of a slowdown in AI spending."The recent decline in AI-linked equities appears driven by market concerns regarding the scale of returns on capital relative to significant capital expenditures and expectations of a slowdown in AI spending," the brokerage said.The shift in global flows has coincided with an improvement in India's domestic macroeconomic environment. Crude oil prices have declined, US 10-year Treasury yields have eased from 5.3% to around 5.1%, and multiple rating agencies have upgraded their GDP growth forecasts for India.The rupee's appreciation against the US dollar has also supported foreign investor returns. BNP Paribas noted that the USD/INR exchange rate moved from 95.8 to 94.3, further enhancing dollar-denominated returns for FIIs.The improvement in investor sentiment has also been reflected in market performance. The Nifty gained around 10.5% over the past month, significantly outperforming the midcap index, which rose 3.7%, and the smallcap index, which gained just 0.5%.IT, telecom lead initial foreign buyingThe initial return of foreign investors was concentrated in the information technology and telecommunications sectors.ALSO READ: Saw the rally coming? How India's mutual funds raised stakes in 11 Nifty stocks before rebound to gain bigAccording to BNP Paribas, NSDL data showed that FII buying in the second half of October was heavily concentrated in these two sectors. Foreign investor holdings in Indian IT stocks increased to $45 billion in October from $37 billion in September, while telecom holdings rose to $39 billion from $35 billion.However, the report noted that market performance in November indicated that the rally had started broadening beyond these sectors into the wider largecap universe.FII holdings in Indian equities stood at $685 billion in October, marginally lower than $689 billion in September, indicating that the recent return of buying had yet to translate into a meaningful month-on-month increase in overall holdings.Largecaps emerge as beneficiariesThe return of foreign investors has coincided with a shift in domestic investor preferences towards largecap stocks, providing an additional source of support to the segment.Flows into pure largecap mutual funds increased around 20% month-on-month to Rs 10 billion in October, while inflows into large and midcap funds surged 99% to Rs 85 billion. In contrast, growth in inflows into midcap and smallcap funds decelerated by 38% and 29%, respectively.BNP Paribas said, "We continue to prefer large caps," arguing that the segment was benefiting from the twin tailwinds of FII buying and retail investors shifting allocations away from small- and midcap-oriented schemes.The investment bank added that the convergence of foreign and domestic buying was providing a significant advantage to largecap valuations."We observe a twin tailwind for Indian large-cap stocks driven by shifting investor flows," the brokerage said, adding that the convergence of FII and retail buying was providing a significant advantage to largecap valuations.Valuations are also relatively more attractive in the largecap segment. The report puts largecap valuations at 18.4 times price-to-earnings, compared with 23.1 times for midcaps and 21.8 times for smallcaps.Largecap earnings growth of around 20% year-on-year in the second quarter of FY27 has also helped narrow the earnings growth gap with smaller companies.Domestic flows remain supportive, but liquidity is tighteningWhile foreign investors have returned, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) have continued to play an important role in supporting the market.DIIs bought $6.5 billion worth of equities in October, even as FIIs sold $2.2 billion during the month. However, domestic mutual fund flows moderated, with overall equity scheme inflows declining 14% month-on-month to Rs 330 billion in October. Systematic investment plan (SIP) inflows remained relatively stable, declining 1% to Rs 321 billion.At the same time, mutual fund cash holdings declined to $18.4 billion, or 3.8% of assets under management, the lowest level since July 2024.BNP Paribas described the shift in domestic investor allocations as a "flight to quality", adding that the rotation from SMID stocks towards largecaps, alongside increased inflows into liquid funds, suggested that investors were becoming more cautious.The brokerage noted that 95% of bond fund inflows were concentrated in liquid and money market funds, indicating a growing preference for cash management.The report also flagged elevated equity supply, with IPOs and qualified institutional placements remaining high for the third consecutive month.Despite the moderation in mutual fund flows, retail participation remained visible, with 3.4 million new demat accounts opened during the month, the highest monthly addition since January 2026.However, the ratio of discontinued or completed SIPs to new registrations increased to 1.17, with new SIP registrations falling to 5.1 million and discontinued SIPs rising to 5.9 million.BNP Paribas cautioned that a sustained reading above one in the SIP stoppage ratio could be negative for future SIP flows.The return of foreign investors, therefore, comes at a time when domestic flows remain substantial but signs of tightening liquidity are emerging within the mutual fund industry.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: India's sugar output more than doubles to 2.35 mn tonnes by Nov 15: ISMA
items.summary:
India's sugar production more than doubled to 23.59 lakh tonne in the ongoing 2026-27 season through November 15, as mills in top producer Maharashtra started crushing early, the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) said on Monday.
Output stood at 11.49 lakh tonne in the same period a year earlier, the industry body said. The sugar season runs from October to September, with crushing typically starting in October-November.
The sweetener's production in Maharashtra, the country's biggest producer, jumped more than threefold to 18.51 lakh tonne from 5.25 lakh tonne a year earlier. Mills in the western state began crushing from October 8, earlier than in other states, and 154 mills were operating as of November 15, against 132 a year ago.
Output in Uttar Pradesh, the second-biggest producer, fell to 2.10 lakh tonne from 4.25 lakh tonne, with 80 mills operational compared with 88 a year earlier.
In Karnataka, the third-largest producer, output was little changed .

Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Inc, USA, on Monday announced the launch of Axitinib Tablets in 1 mg and 5 mg strengths, a generic version of Pfizer Inc's Inlyta tablets.
Glenmark Axitinib tablets (a generic equivalent to Pfizer's Inlyta) are used to treat advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC), a type of kidney cancer.
"The launch of Axitinib tablets reinforces Glenmark's commitment to expanding access to quality, affordable medicines for patients in the United States," said Marc Kikuchi, President & Business Head, North America.
By adding this product to its portfolio, the company continues to strengthen focus on addressing the evolving needs of patients and healthcare providers, he said .
According to IQVIA sales data for the 12-month period ended September 2026, annual sales of Inlyta tablets in the US were around USD 538.4 million, the company said in a statement.

items.title: Belrise Industries shares jump 11% as Q2 profit rises 25% YoY; revenue grows 17%
items.summary: Belrise Industries shares rallied 10.50% to Rs 237.78 during Monday’s trading session after the company reported 25% year-on-year (YoY) growth in profit after tax (PAT) and a 17% increase in revenue from operations for the September quarter (Q2 FY27).Belrise Industries Limited (BIL), an integrated automotive component manufacturer, announced its financial results for Q2 FY27 and the first half of FY27, reporting growth in both revenue and profitability.The company's revenue from operations increased 17% YoY to Rs 2,746 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,353 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 25% to Rs 166 crore from Rs 133 crore in Q2 FY26.Belrise Industries Q2 FY27 business highlightsThe company's manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 18,601 million in the year-ago quarter. Manufacturing EBITDA increased 19% to Rs 3,170 million from Rs 2,663 million in Q2 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.5% during the quarter. Additionally, 71% of the company's manufacturing revenue came from powertrain-neutral products.Belrise Industries H1 FY27 performanceFor the first half of FY27, manufacturing revenue increased 23% YoY to Rs 45,420 million, compared with Rs 36,923 million in H1 FY26. Manufacturing EBITDA rose 15% to Rs 5,963 million from Rs 5,199 million in the corresponding period last year. The manufacturing EBITDA margin stood at 13.1%, while powertrain-neutral products accounted for 71% of manufacturing revenue.Belrise Industries secures new ordersDuring the quarter, Belrise Industries secured several new orders across its commercial vehicle and two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses. The company won a programme from a leading Indian commercial vehicle manufacturer to supply complete chassis frame assemblies across its heavy commercial vehicle (HCV) platforms. The supplies will be made from a new facility in Dharwad, with production expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28.The programme is expected to add Rs 60,000–1 lakh in content per vehicle, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,500–2,000 million.Belrise also entered complete three-wheeler body manufacturing after being selected as the second source for complete body and chassis assemblies for a high-selling model of a leading Indian two-wheeler and three-wheeler manufacturer. The order represents incremental content of approximately Rs 9,000 per vehicle.Production from its new facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is expected to ramp up from Q1 FY28, with peak annual revenue potential of Rs 1,000–1,200 million.In its suspension business, the company onboarded its sixth original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customer, a leading premium two-wheeler manufacturer in South India. Supplies commenced in Q3 FY27. It also secured additional orders from a growing two-wheeler and three-wheeler OEM, with production expected to begin in Q4 FY27.What management saidCommenting on the company's Q2 and H1 FY27 performance, Shrikant Badve, Managing Director of Belrise Industries, said the quarter was marked by strong execution and a healthy demand environment. He highlighted that manufacturing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 23,441 million, while adjusted PAT increased 25% to Rs 1,663 million.Also read: Tata Motors PV shares crack 9% as Motilal Oswal cuts earnings estimates, stays bearish after Q2 resultsThe company also secured its maiden Letter of Intent (LoI) for the supply of CNC fixtures to an ecosystem partner of one of the largest American smartphone companies.According to Badve, India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem is poised to become one of the country's largest and most cost-competitive manufacturing segments. The new order will provide Belrise with an opportunity to demonstrate its precision engineering capabilities developed over the years.Share PriceBelrise Industries shares have rallied 45% over the past one year. The stock is currently trading at a market capitalisation of Rs 21,567 crore. This comes after the renewable energy player reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 58.83 crore for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027, marking around 36% year-on-year decline from Rs 91.75 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.The company’s revenue from operations increased more than 21% YoY to Rs 1,354 crore during the quarter under review, from Rs 1,119 crore reported in the same period last year. Total expenses meanwhile increased more than 28% YoY to Rs 1,275 crore. Also Read | India Inc’s Q2 profit jumps 26%; auto, financials, oil & gas lead growthInox Wind’s EBITDA dropped more than 22% YoY to Rs 238 crore, from Rs 306 crore in Q2 of FY26, with the EBITDA margin slowing to 17%. The company however said this does not reflect the true picture as income from wind world O&M portfolio has not been recognised in the earnings for this quarter. The company’s management acknowledged that the earlier FY27 guidance of around 75% YoY revenue growth is unlikely to be achieved and has shifted its focus to FY28, with revenue guidance of Rs 7,500 crore.Additionally, Inox Wind announced that its CEO Sanjeev Agarwal has resigned due to personal reasons, while former Vikram Solar CEO Saibaba Vutukuri has been appointed as the Managing Director of of Inox Wind’s wind business.Motilal Oswal on Inox Wind share priceMotilal Oswal Financial Services reduced its target price for Inox Wind shares to Rs 74 apiece, while maintaining its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock. The target price implies around 15% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 64.45 apiece on NSE.The domestic brokerage said the company’s consolidated revenue came in 7% above estimates, while EBITDA missed expectations by 5%. It noted that WindWorld’s acquisition, 3.8GW order book providing over 24 months of execution visibility, supplemented by a healthy 5 GW near-term tender pipeline, and recurring opportunities from Inox Clean Energy are some of the things it liked from the earnings print.Motilal Oswal however noted that the lowering of guidance, timely consolidation of WindWorld from Q3 FY27 and execution of margin improvement initiatives, as well as benefits from the strategic shift toward equipment supply need to translate into lower working capital intensity and improved cash conversion, are the key monitorables. The domestic brokerage cut FY27 and FY28 EBITDA estimated for Inox Wind by 21% and 14% respectively, factoring in lower estimated deliveries and moderated EBITDA margins of 18% and 19%.Also read | Jefferies' Chris Wood sees fresh US-Iran tensions as biggest risk to India, sees this sector as the best hedgeInox Wind share priceInox Wind shares dropped more than 11% in a week and nearly 13% in one month, with the stock overall being down around 52% in 2026 so far and 60% in one year. In the longer term, Inox Wind shares have fallen more than 5% in three years but delivered positive returns of more than 78% in five years. Jimmy Tata accuses Noel of 'backdoor takeover'
items.summary: Jimmy Naval Tata, younger brother of late Ratan Tata and one of the longest-serving trustees of Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), has accused Noel Tata of using the charitable institutions to consolidate family control over Tata Sons, calling the induction of multiple family members into the trusts a “back-door takeover” of the group’s holding company.In a detailed written response to a senior trustee on the state of affairs at Tata Trusts and controversies surrounding the group, Jimmy has also criticised changes to Tata Sons’ Articles of Association, backed chairman N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and called on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to enforce the listing of Tata Sons without delay.Also Read: Jimmy Tata breaks silence on Tata matters; backs Chandra staying chair & Tata Sons listing, opposing Noel's stance“What has transpired in recent time is that the trusts are being filled with family members of the present Tata Trust Chairman, thereby securing a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlors’ intention,” he said, adding that having more than one family member on a trust was inappropriate.“Such an arrangement is untenable and amounts to a back-door takeover of Tata Sons,” he said.Jimmy’s intervention is significant as the 85-year-old trustee has largely stayed away from trust meetings and voting and has rarely publicly articulated his views on the ongoing differences within the group.He said the two principal Tata trusts were established by Sir Ratan Tata and Sir Dorabji Tata for public welfare and that trustees were custodians of their assets, not owners. He cited their founding objectives, including poverty alleviation and safeguarding Indian culture, and said the institutions should remain focused on serving the people of India.Jimmy traced the current governance differences to amendments made to Tata Sons’ Articles of Association around 2013-14, which he said had fundamentally altered the relationship between the charitable trusts and the operating company.He argued that the earlier framework kept the welfare trusts separate from Tata Sons’ commercial operations, while subsequent amendments gave the Tata Trusts chairman veto powers and the ability to place directors, undermining the collective authority of the board.He also questioned differences in trustee tenure rules, alleging that they had compromised independence and enabled the marginalisation of dissenting trustees.Also Read: Noel Tata warns Tata Sons listing could put profits ahead of philanthropy, says it may change the ‘Tata way’Citing Venu Srinivasan, whose term expires in December, he alleged that Srinivasan was being targeted for opposing the induction of Noel Tata’s son into SRTT. He also referred to the earlier removal of Vijay Singh.Jimmy contrasted the current situation with the past, when independent figures such as Nani Palkhivala, Gautam Sarabhai, Homi Sethna and Homi Bhabha served as trustees.On the differences over Chandrasekaran’s continuation as Tata Sons chairman, Jimmy praised his leadership, saying he had turned around companies burdened by severe debt and delivered record earnings and substantial dividend payouts.“Despite Chandrasekaran receiving overwhelming support (including 4–1 in Tata Sons board and a unanimous resolution passed by Tata Trusts), Noel sought to block him arbitrarily by invoking the onerous veto provisions in the amended Articles of Association without providing any justification or accountability,” he said.Jimmy’s comments come amid a widening rift between Noel, chairman of Tata Trusts, and the Tata Sons board over Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, the proposed listing of the holding company and the group’s governance structure.Tata Trusts collectively owns about 66% of Tata Sons, with SRTT holding 23.56%. Its position is central to decisions concerning the future of the holding company and the wider conglomerate.Jimmy said listing Tata Sons was critical to improving transparency and accountability and restoring the separation between the charitable trusts and the commercial operations of the group.“Listing would dismantle the pervasive culture of secrecy, impose statutory accountability, and necessitate rewriting the onerous Articles of Association to restore the pre-1989 separation between business operations and welfare trusts,” he said.He also warned against any attempt to restructure Tata Sons into smaller entities to avoid regulatory listing requirements, saying this would be contrary to public and shareholder interests.Jimmy called on the RBI to enforce strict timelines for listing and urged the government and the Charity Commissioner to intervene to protect the original objectives of the trusts.The RBI has classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company (NBFC), requiring it to list its equity shares on a recognised stock exchange within three years of being identified in that category. The central bank has rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its core investment company registration, requiring it to comply with the regulatory framework applicable to upper-layer NBFCs.Also Read: Tata International appoints T V Narendran as Chairman and Noel N Tata as Chairman Emeritus effective November 12Jimmy has been a trustee of SRTT since 1989 and is one of its three perpetual trustees, the others being Noel Tata and Jehangir Jehangir. He is the younger son of Naval Tata and his first wife Sooni Commissariat. Noel Tata is Naval Tata’s son from his second marriage to Simone Dunoyer.Jimmy, who lives in Pune, has historically preferred correspondence to participation in trust meetings. During a 2016 interview, he showed reporters a file containing hundreds of letters through which he had communicated his views to trustees and board members.He is also the second-largest individual shareholder of Tata Sons after Noel Tata, with a 0.81% stake, or 3,262 shares, according to estimates based on investment banking data.

items.title: FPI buying hits 5-year high in November. What's driving the $7.5 billion inflow?
items.summary: Mumbai: In a sharp U-turn after months of sustained selling, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pumped $7.5 billion into Indian equities in the first 10 trading sessions of November - the highest monthly inflow in five years, according to Bloomberg data.This comes after FPIs withdrew $2.17 billion from Indian equities in October and $3.46 billion in September. The net investments in November so far are the highest since November 2021. The last time foreign investors pumped in more money in a single month was November 2020, when inflows stood at $9.56 billion, the data showed.135868866According to fund managers, FPIs have been aggressively investing amid a correction in AI-related stocks globally and a decline in crude oil prices. "The FPI flows are driven by multiple factors. profit booking on AI Investments, drop in oil prices, election results in Brazil, correction in Indian valuations over last two years, talks of exemptions on capital gains and reduction in rupee volatility," said Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra AMC.All this came in quick succession and the combined effect is visible in FPI flows, he said.Read more: IPO calendar: Mahanadi Coalfields among 3 companies to raise over Rs 10,000 cr in busy week for primary marketBrent crude prices have fallen nearly 21% to $93.37 per barrel on November 13 from a peak of $118 on October 30. The Indian rupee has appreciated by ₹1.97, or about 2%, against the US dollar since the beginning of October, rising from ₹96.22 per dollar to ₹94.25 per dollar by mid-November.Domestic institutional investors, meanwhile, have turned net sellers, booking profits amid a sharp rally in the market, after providing a crucial backstop through much of the year. DIIs have sold equities worth over ₹49,000 crore in the first 10 trading sessions of November, according to NSE data. Since the beginning of November, the Sensex and Nifty have gained nearly 10% each, while the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices have advanced around 8% each.Read more: Will Sensex, Nifty continue their bull run or consolidate? 4 factors to watch out for this weekOverseas investors began 2026 with net outflows of $3.26 billion into Indian equities in January, before turning net buyers in February with investments of $1.69 billion. However, the respite was short-lived, as March saw a sharp reversal, with FPIs pulling out $13.23 billion - their biggest monthly sell-off.Their return to Indian equities reflects both global portfolio rotation away from AI-heavy markets and improving outlook for India, said Anurag Byas, director for global markets solutions at Rothschild & Co. "Lower crude prices, better earnings and now attractive valuations seem to have supported this sentiment change. This is a positive signal but may be early to be extrapolated; the fundamentals must improve and the oil and currency stability must hold for this to become a sustained trend," he said. Shah of Kotak Mahindra AMC expects FPI flows to move in line with how the above factors interplay with each other.

Peak repo rate pegged lower at 6%, Dec hike on
items.summary: Mumbai: The rate-hike cycle is now expected to be shallower than previously anticipated, provided relatively softer crude oil prices and an easing of geopolitical tensions in West Asia persist into 2027, say economists.Most economists expect the terminal, or peak, repo rate at 6%, reversing earlier projections of 6.25%. While some still see the possibility of the policy rate rising to 6.25%, they consider it a low-probability outcome that would depend entirely on incoming data.Also Read: Food inflation to stay elevated; ICICI Bank sees 25 bps RBI rate hike in DecemberA rate hike in December, however, is widely expected, particularly after October retail inflation accelerated to 6.09%, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years.135864578The RBI is legally required to maintain the headline inflation between 2% and 6%.The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is scheduled to announce its rate decision on December 4. The committee raised the policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% at its last meeting in October, citing inflationary risks due to global uncertainties and deficient rains.Also Read: India's consumption story remains strong, but rural demand faces inflation risks: Report"Considering recent developments, we believe that the balance of probabilities has decisively shifted towards a 25-bps rate hike in December. We do not consider a further rate hike in February advisable, given the proximity to the union budget," State Bank of India chief economic adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh wrote in a report last week."The December 25-bps hike to be followed by a more data-dependent policy approach. This also leaves room for a downward revision in terminal-rate expectations," the report said.Indranil Pan, chief economist at Yes Bank said, "A hike in April remains a possibility, but the probability of the same may have weakened due to cooling global crude prices and steadying rupee."Brent prices fell sharply in early November as markets responded to expectations that the US would avoid another major military offensive after Democrats took control of both houses in the US.The recent correction in crude oil prices has tempered expectations of a relatively aggressive hiking cycle, with markets scaling back bets on multiple rate increases in the coming MPC meetings.Domestic inflationary risks also remain, due to the potential impact of El Nino, which could push up food prices. "Inflation has mostly peaked and while upcoming CPI prints may soften, they will continue to stay elevated, paving the way for measured hikes by the MPC. We expect the hiking cycle to be rather shallow," Barclays chief economist Aastha Gudwani said.

items.title: Dems should call Trump’s immigration bluff
items.summary: In casting their ballots for Democrats, voters couldn’t have been clearer about their disgust with Republican Party priorities — including, as even President Donald Trump has admitted, his administration’s overzealous approach to immigration enforcement. “It might be too tough,” he told 60 Minutes last Sunday. Yet Trump has been anything but clear when asked what he plans to do about it.This past week alone, the president has veered from offering to work with Democrats on immigration reform to defending the promotion of immigration hard-liner Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff. Trump said targeting immigrants without criminal records “hurt” Republicans, but also said he’s not making changes. “There won’t be amnesty,” he told reporters. And that’s on top of his administration bragging about hitting new records for deportations. “Thanks to President Trump’s leadership,” Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said, “ICE has been unleashed.”ALSO READ | More companies may face action in H-1B probe, warns US Labour Department's Anthony D’EspositoGiven all the mixed messages, it seems highly unlikely that a fix for the nation’s broken immigration system is coming if Trump gets to dictate the agenda and the timetable. To be sure, a compromise would be ideal. But if anything is to get done on immigration in the next Congress, Democrats will likely have to force the issue, pushing legislation and daring Republicans to filibuster it or Trump to veto it.Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has proposed just such a strategy for making health care more affordable. Trump will have two choices, as Schumer told the Washington Sun. He will either sign what will be very popular legislation — “and he’ll know it’s popular” — or obstruct it, giving Democrats a better chance of winning the presidency in 2028.ALSO READ | IBM's H-1B move, US tech layoffs: Why is it getting harder for Indians to work and settle in America?The same could work for legislation on immigration reform (although it doesn’t seem to be a priority for the House so far). The key for Democrats will be resisting the temptation to go too far left, as some in the party want to do, and instead stick to policies that match public opinion and stand a good chance of improving the economy.Polls show that most Americans appreciate the economic benefits of legal immigration. They want a secure border, but don’t approve of violent enforcement tactics that have left multiple people dead. Americans also favor admitting refugees and asylum seekers fleeing war-torn countries, and providing a viable pathway to citizenship for immigrants who were brought to the US as children, or have been living in the US for years.Depending on the day, Trump will pay lip service to agreeing to much of this. As he told 60 Minutes last Sunday, killers should be deported, but not necessarily “good people working in a landscaping company or working in a hotel” and “paying taxes.”But Trump has said such things before, only to backtrack. He did so in 2017, when he toyed with helping DREAMers — immigrants brought to the US as children — get citizenship. What had seemed like a more solid deal fell apart in 2018 after immigration hard-liners, led by Miller, got involved. Another one fizzled in 2019.Trump has never been a particularly reliable negotiating partner. He breaks promises and changes his mind on a whim. With Miller in Trump’s ear more often now as White House chief of staff, Democrats are right to be skeptical that will change just because Republicans received an electoral beatdown for the ages. Yet Democrats seem to be moving forward anyway, however tentatively.This past week, a group of Latino lawmakers, many of them newly elected to Congress, gathered outside the Capitol to publicly push for immigration reform. Specifically, they called on Trump and Republicans to support the bipartisan Dignity Act and the American Dream and Promise Act, both of which would solve a mix of problems with the current immigration system.“I have very aspirational dreams and hopes for immigration reform. But I am also a pragmatist,” Representative Veronica Escobar of Texas said. “And as we have — as we continue to have — Donald Trump in the White House, and without a supermajority in the Senate, we need Republican support. So any comprehensive immigration reform must be bipartisan.”Senator Ruben Gallego of Arizona said congressional Democrats had a responsibility to “protect as many families as possible,” even if that means “potentially cutting a deal with Donald Trump.”A smaller group of Latino business leaders who also spoke at the Capitol were more direct and, dare I say, more realistic. They reminded the Trump administration that its policy of mass deportations has disrupted the economy, forcing businesses to close and workers to stay home, forfeiting their paychecks. This has been as true in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas as it has been in southwestern Kansas. And it had a lot to do with Republican Latino voters abandoning Trump.In a warning to the administration, Benny Melendez, vice chair of the South Texas Builders Association, said to nods from Latino lawmakers: “If you want to continue harassing our communities, prepare yourself not only to lose your job, but get ready, because in the 2028 elections, these same communities you are now harassing will make sure you lose the White House.”The reality is, Trump may never compromise on legislation. That shouldn’t stop Democrats from advancing a vision of what a well-run immigration system could look like, and explaining how that could ease everything from the housing shortage that’s driving up costs to labor shortages at meatpacking plants and farms that threaten to raise grocery prices even more.If Democrats can present a plan that’s in line with what most Americans want, there’s a good chance voters will reward them for it — and punish Republicans for standing in the way. Just because the Trump administration is in disarray over immigration doesn’t mean Democrats have to be as well.The views expressed in this article are the author's own and do not necessarily reflect the views of the publication.

Delhi AQI dips to 290, but relief may be brief
items.summary: Following days of toxic, post-Diwali smog blanketing the national capital, Delhi's air quality improved slightly to the 'poor' category on Sunday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching 290 by 4 pm.Across the city's 58 monitoring stations, 34 registered 'poor' air quality and 23 logged 'very poor', leaving only Delhi Cantonment in the 'moderate' zone. NSIT Dwarka recorded the capital's worst air, with an AQI of 364. Earlier that morning, the Sameer app had placed the city's air in the 'very poor' bracket at 350.Per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) scale, an AQI of 0–50 is 'good', 51–100 is 'satisfactory', 101–200 is 'moderate', 201–300 is 'poor', 301–400 is 'very poor', and 401–500 is 'severe'. Delhi had been stuck in the 'very poor' tier continuously since November 11, with hourly readings repeatedly nearing, and once breaching, the 'severe' threshold. Prior to Sunday, the last 'poor' AQI reading was 299 on November 10, preceded by 261 on November 1.Real-time PM2.5 source apportionment data from the Air Quality Early Warning System and the Integrated Decision Support System identified biomass burning, encompassing stubble burning, domestic solid biofuels, wood, and dung cakes—as Sunday's primary pollutant source at 37.1 per cent. Secondary organic aerosols, which are fine particulates generated by atmospheric gas reactions, ranked second at 22 per cent, trailed by vehicular emissions (17.2 per cent) and secondary inorganic aerosols (9.6 per cent). Smaller shares came from waste burning, such as municipal, plastic, and rubber waste (5.5 per cent), mixed combustion (4.3 per cent), mineral dust and ash (2 per cent), firecrackers (1.6 per cent), and industrial emissions (0.6 per cent).This relief is expected to be brief. According to the Air Quality Early Warning System, Delhi's air will likely stay 'poor' on November 16 before deteriorating back to 'very poor' on November 17 and 18, remaining in that bracket for the following six days.Meteorologists credited Sunday's temporary dip in pollution to light rain and stronger winds helping disperse trapped pollutants. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) noted that parts of Delhi experienced drizzle or very light rain over the preceding 24 hours, accompanied by southwesterly surface winds peaking at 15 kmph. Skies were mostly cloudy before turning partly cloudy by afternoon, with southwesterly winds blowing up to 10 kmph.However, the IMD's forecast bulletin projects the city's ventilation index to drop steadily, from 16,000 square metres per second on November 15 to 15,000 on November 16, 7,500 on November 17, and 6,000 on November 18. The bulletin noted that a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, combined with average wind speeds under 10 kmph, creates poor conditions for dispersing pollutants.

Bangladesh unrest shuts garment factories
items.summary: Dhaka: Fresh labour unrest hit Bangladesh's garment industry on Sunday, with 13 factories shut indefinitely and five others declaring a one-day holiday, a day before the wage board is due to meet to continue consultations on recommending a revised pay structure.Protesting workers gathered in Gazipur's Konabari and Mouchak areas, prompting police to use tear gas and sound grenades to disperse them. Factory owners said 50 units in the industrial zone were closed.Also Read: Floppy disks, paper strips and ageing computers: America's aviation system is stuck in the pastThe latest disruption comes amid weeks of protests over workers' demand to raise the minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka (USD 100) to 30,000 taka (USD 240), with demonstrations and factory shutdowns reported across key industrial belts.Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for over 80 per cent of the country's export earnings, making prolonged disruption a concern for international buyers and global supply chains.Also Read: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo 6 months into responseThe government formed a Minimum Wage Board on November 1 to recommend a revised pay structure. The board, chaired by a senior district judge, agreed at its first meeting to finalise its recommendations by the end of November.The revised pay structure is expected to take effect from December 1, with workers set to receive their first salaries under the new scale in January.The fresh unrest on Sunday came a day after garment factory owners warned of indefinite, unpaid closures at factories where workers refused to resume production.Police and factory owners said 13 readymade garment factories were shut for an indefinite period, while five others declared a one-day general holiday in Gazipur and nearby Ashulia.Workers at a garment factory rallied in Gazipur's Konabari area, prompting police to rush to the scene and disperse them using tear gas and sound grenades at around 8.30 am local time.Workers from other factories later took to the streets in the adjacent Mouchak area, forcing management to close their units."Workers made attempts to gather at different locations this morning, but law enforcement personnel prevented them with their prompt actions and remain deployed at every key point in the industrial area," Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amzad Hossain said.Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said it had deployed 13 platoons of paramilitary personnel to maintain order and protect factories, alongside police in riot gear and the elite Special Response Battalion (SRB), which draws personnel from the army, navy, air force and police.Gazipur district administration officials said several platoons of the Ansar battalion had also been called out to guard the factories. They said 25 executive magistrates had been assigned to lead law enforcement personnel.Factory owners said 50 garment units were closed in the industrial zone, including 13 shut on Sunday amid fresh unrest.Officials said production continued at most factories in Gazipur's industrial belt despite the disruption.The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said its representatives would attend the minimum wage board meeting on Monday to submit their proposal, despite reluctance among some of its members.The BGMEA, however, warned that its participation in subsequent meetings would depend on how the situation on the ground unfolded.The continued protests have centred on demands for a "living wage to survive", with workers saying their earnings have not kept pace with rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare.Factory owners have warned that prolonged disruption during the peak production season for spring and summer orders could delay shipments, affect overseas buyers' confidence and lead to cancellations.Bangladesh supplies major international fashion brands, including H&M, Zara and Gap. The sector has also faced pressure from rising production costs, inflation and intense competition in global markets.The protests turned violent in the first week of November, with demonstrators setting ablaze police vans and public transport vehicles and blocking two major highways.Ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) activists also took to the streets in anti-protest campaigns, carrying bamboo sticks to maintain order and resist what they described as "infiltrators".BNP leaders have accused Hasina and her supporters of trying to destabilise the government through the protests, while the former prime minister has rejected such allegations in media interviews.Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's information affairs adviser, Zahedur Rahman, earlier accused the deposed premier of fuelling the unrest, saying, "Sheikh Hasina will not let the government remain in peace as long as she is alive".A student-led uprising toppled Hasina's government on August 5, 2024, forcing her to flee to India. The interim government led by Muhammad Yunus later disbanded the Awami League under anti-terrorism legislation.

items.title: Crypto’s slow-motion selloff leaves traders weary and hopeless
items.summary: Bitcoin’s latest selloff is testing the resolve of some of the cryptocurrency market’s most committed investors, as a succession of setbacks pushes prices toward their lowest levels of the year and major sources of demand weaken.The largest digital asset fell toward $62,000 in weekend trading, reaching its weakest level since July, extending a decline that has gathered pace in recent weeks. Unlike the abrupt crashes that have punctuated previous crypto downturns, much of the preceding decline unfolded during relatively subdued trading before liquidations accelerated in recent days.The steady erosion is adding to a sense of exhaustion across a market confronting a growing list of obstacles, from the record hack at Binance and renewed political uncertainty following Democratic gains in the US midterm elections to rising Treasury yields and a stronger dollar. Meanwhile, the artificial-intelligence boom and Anthropic’s upcoming IPO are competing for money and attention once directed toward digital assets.“The near-term direction will largely depend on whether institutional demand stabilizes and macro conditions provide room for risk appetite to recover,” said Ayesha Kiani, chief operating officer at Monarq Asset Management. “Until then, rallies are likely to remain fragile and volatility elevated.”135852805US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which helped draw Wall Street investors into the market, have become another source of selling pressure. From Oct. 30 — the day after the Binance hack — through Nov. 13, the ETFs saw almost $3 billion in net outflows.Economic conditions offer little relief. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries has climbed above 5% as persistent inflation fueled expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy. Higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding assets that generate no income, while the stronger dollar has added pressure to Bitcoin and gold.Crypto-specific developments have compounded the weakness.The Binance hack has revived questions about the security of trading platforms at a time when the industry is struggling to rebuild investor confidence. The competition for speculative capital is also intensifying. Anthropic’s planned initial public offering has attracted heavy demand ahead of its expected listing, raising the possibility that investors are freeing up money from other holdings, including cryptocurrencies, to participate. The extent of any direct shift out of digital assets remains unclear.“Theories around the market weakness tend to focus on the large outflows of stablecoin balances, nearly $20 billion over the last month, the upcoming IPO of Anthropic and its impact on liquidity,” said Joshua Lim, co-head of markets at FalconX.Bitcoin’s retreat is particularly frustrating for investors who had expected mainstream adoption to provide a more durable foundation for prices. Major financial institutions have expanded their involvement in digital assets, and ETFs have made Bitcoin available to a much broader pool of investors. Those advances have not insulated the market from its latest downturn.Many smaller digital tokens have surrendered years of gains, challenging the returns available to investors who held through successive industry booms and busts.For traders looking for a potential floor, August offers one reference point.After risk appetite improved following the US Treasury’s announcement of an increase in long-bond buybacks, Bitcoin rallied from below $65,000 to above $87,000 by late September. The latest decline has erased most of those gains and raised the prospect of a further slide under the roughly $58,000 level that has marked this year’s low.“We’re in a risk-off environment across all financial markets. Interest rates keep rising with the war still pressuring inflation,” said Ryan Watkins, co-founder of crypto investment fund Syncracy Capital.
