Why Indians behave better at sacred sites
items.summary: The tranquil and indescribably beautiful environs of Kamarpukur and Joyrambati, the birthplaces of Sri Ramkrishna Paramhansa and Maa Sarada Devi in the verdant plains of West Bengal, are truly balms for the soul. Green-gold vistas of ripening rice fields criss-crossed by a myriad of small rivers and dotted with distant sleepy hamlets greeted the eye as a friend and I headed there from Kolkata. And the early morning autumn sun cast a golden, almost divine glow.It was a world away from the pollution-spewing trucks and buses, factories and warehouses that crowd the suburbs of Kolkata beyond the graceful Vidyasagar Setu arching over the Hooghly. Once the cacophony of the Durgapur Expressway was left behind, there was a perceptible change in mood. Anyone who lives in a frenetic big city these days would vouch that stress is endemic and heading out, away from the madding crowds, leads to an instant lowering of tension.Also Read: Indians splurge Rs 72k cr on their favourite obsessionAnd peace is the overwhelming feeling upon entering the impeccably maintained compounds in both villages that contain not only the quaintly thatched huts where the two elevated souls came into this world, but also prayer halls, offices, bhog areas, dispensaries, guesthouses and flower-filled gardens. Given that thousands - exceeding 20,000 on important days - visit Kamarpukur and Joyrambati daily and stay on for bhog prasad, the compounds' serenity is hard to believe.And their cleanliness stuns. Forget jhalmuri packets, tissue papers or plastic water bottles, not even fallen leaves or dust mar the pathways and gardens. It is not as if there are armies of sweepers on hand to pick up detritus either; visitors are simply more mindful while on the premises. How come? After all Indians these days are notorious for being loud, littering gits, on par with British lager louts. It seems that it all depends on whether places inspire respect and restraint.Also Read: India says foreign goods can overstayIn the expansive hallowed campuses of Kamarpukur and Joyrambati, these same people - Indians - did not talk loudly; they did not try to scratch their initials on pillars; they did not drape themselves on walls or amid the flowers to take selfies; they did not throw trash into the ponds; and they did not let their children turn into screeching, high-speed, wrecking balls. Polite attendants firmly told the few infringers to abide by the rules. And they all willingly complied.I have seen a similar all-pervasive calm at the Belur Math of the Ramakrishna Mission near Kolkata, the Aurobindo Ashram in Pondicherry and the Golden Temple in Amritsar, thousands of miles apart. There are more such places around India where desi visitors are anything but the kind of Ugly Indian Tourist that locals complain about from Goa to Gangtok, Kashmir to Kanyakumari. That just begs the question why Indians are so badly behaved in many other places.An overwhelming majority of those who come to Kamarpukur and Joyrambati are devotees. They, therefore, know the sanctity of those places and behave accordingly. The same is true of the sacred precincts at Belur, Pondicherry and Amritsar. But why is the same courtesy not extended to all places they visit? Do only the divine merit courtesy, cleanliness and calm? The public's behaviour at these places show that Indians can be model visitors when we want to be.At Kamarpukur and Joyrambati it is hard to be anything but ideal visitors, though. There's something about the cumulative effect of their soothing tranquillity broken only by birdsong and trees rustling in the autumn breeze, the fresh flowers artfully arranged around the statues of Sri Ramkrishna and Maa Sarada Devi, and the smiling sanyasis telling stories of the divine couple's limitless humanity and humbleness... On the journey back to Kolkata, our hearts were full.

Jensen Huang controversy puts Southeast Asia’s AI chip trade under scrutiny
items.summary: Chip and data-centre operators in Southeast Asia are bracing for tighter scrutiny after reports linking former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to a Chinese businesswoman suspected of spying for Beijing put Singapore and Malaysia in the spotlight, industry executives and analysts told Reuters.The controversy has prompted US lawmakers from both parties to push for stronger restrictions on China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s role in US national security.Washington already restricts exports of Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips to China to protect US leadership in the sector. Lawmakers are now seeking to close a loophole that allows Chinese companies to rent computing power from overseas data centres and remotely access systems equipped with restricted chips.Any tougher regulations could include new export controls and licensing requirements for shipments to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, the Wall Street Journal reported.Also Read | Anthropic IPO share orders from China are said to be rebuffedAlice Huang, the businesswoman suspected of spying for China, previously worked as an executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed. The company has subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Australia and the US.Singapore authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since February last year over possible false declarations related to server purchases and other alleged offences.“After this case, every operator in the chain will be expected to know its end user. Southeast Asian operators will still get Nvidia chips, but proof of where every chip sits and who it serves is now part of the product,” Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based investment research firm Shenton Research, told Reuters.A ‘post-DeepSeek moment’Southeast Asia’s data-centre industry has grown rapidly as global technology companies expand their AI infrastructure.Malaysia has approved 385.7 billion ringgit ($94.67 billion) of data-centre-related investment since 2021, according to the country’s trade ministry. Thailand had 42 data centres representing 3,400 megawatts of IT capacity and about 750 billion baht ($22.58 billion) of investment as of February, while Indonesia’s market was valued at $2.81 billion in 2025.Gary Goh, CEO of Malaysia-based data-centre consultancy Sprint DC, described the prospect of tighter US rules as a “post-DeepSeek moment.”“Once the new rules are out, there will be a lot more restrictions for countries like Malaysia. There could be a short- to medium-term market shock to the Malaysian data centre market,” Goh said.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe AI boom has supported economic growth across the region. Singapore raised its annual growth forecast in August to between 4.5% and 5.5%, from 2% to 4%, citing the AI cycle. In Malaysia, an increase in data-centre projects helped the construction sector grow 6% in the third quarter of 2026.The trade ministries of Singapore and Malaysia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Malaysia said Thursday that it was considering legislation that would allow the government to monitor data-centre operations, including the use of high-performance chips. Authorities said they needed to ensure that chips subject to US restrictions were imported for domestic use rather than re-exported.An investor and CEO of an Asian neocloud company, who asked not to be identified, said he spent Friday morning consulting lawyers in the US.“Everyone is still figuring out... Maybe every time you export something, there will be additional process to go through. We are worried about more scrutiny which will make it longer for chips to come through,” the CEO said.Singapore said in February 2025 that entities operating in the country accounted for 22% of Nvidia’s chip sales, although only 1% of the chips physically entered Singapore. Authorities have also charged a fifth person in a case involving alleged AI-server fraud.Region expected to withstand tighter rulesSome analysts said tighter controls were unlikely to derail the data-centre expansion in Singapore and Malaysia.“Singapore itself will be more stringent; I think it’s a natural thing to happen. Singapore will tighten rules, and the US will tighten rules, but I don’t think this will harm Singapore’s and Malaysia’s prospects of buying chips,”  Jarick Seet, head of small- and mid-cap equities at Maybank, told Reuters.A senior executive at a Singapore chipmaker, who declined to be identified, said Huang’s departure could make it more difficult for Chinese companies to obtain US chips while potentially improving availability elsewhere.“With Jensen out, the Chinese will have a harder time getting chips from the US. Maybe it is not a bad thing for the non-US people who will have more access to chips.”The executive said companies could also redirect investment to Southeast Asia if Democratic electoral victories in data-centre-heavy US states such as Texas and Georgia slow the development of new facilities.“Those companies are going to look elsewhere and likely come to countries that can offer them land and deals and power,” the executive said. “Even if we lose a chunk of the China business, I think we will get other companies coming looking for compute.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: India imports over half its edible oil, faces food risks: NITI Aayog VC
items.summary:
India is perhaps still not secure regarding its food supply across the various products, as the country is the world's largest importer of edible oils, NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said on Friday.
Addressing an event here, Lahiri said India meets more than half of its edible oil needs through imports, and imports are estimated at 17 million metric tonnes, valued at about USD 20 billion.
Similarly, India is both the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses, and accounts for roughly a fourth of total global pulse consumption, approximately 25 to 27 million tonnes annually.

items.title: India says foreign goods can overstay
items.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)  introduced greater flexibility for foreign businesses and organisations on Friday, bringing goods into India temporarily by allowing senior customs officials to extend the existing four-month stay limit under the ATA Carnet system.The move will benefit foreign exhibitors, businesses, media organisations and other international participants who need to bring equipment, commercial samples or professional goods into India for a limited period. Until now, such goods were generally required to be re-exported within four months of their import.Under the revised provision, Principal Chief Commissioners of Customs and Chief Commissioners of Customs can approve an extension beyond the four months if they consider it necessary in the public interest.However, the extended period cannot go beyond the validity of the respective ATA Carnet."Provided also that where the Principal Chief Commissioner of Customs or the Chief Commissioner of Customs, as the case may be, is satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest so to do, may extend the aforesaid period of four months by such further period as it may deem fit, not exceeding the period of validity of the A.T.A. Carnet," said a memo from the Department of Revenue.What changes under the revised ATA Carnet rules?The amendment gives senior customs officials the authority to grant additional time for temporarily imported goods to remain in India.Previously, the four-month limit applied under the relevant customs notification, leaving limited room for businesses and organisations that needed more time before sending their goods back.With the latest change, the Principal Chief Commissioner or Chief Commissioner of Customs can assess individual cases and allow an extension where circumstances justify it.The additional time will depend on the official's assessment, but there is one important restriction: the extension must remain within the validity period of the ATA Carnet. This means the new provision does not allow goods to stay in India indefinitely.The amendment has been made to Notification No. 4/2018-Customs, dated January 18, 2018, by inserting an additional proviso under condition (vi).What is the ATA Carnet system and how does it work?An ATA Carnet is an international customs document that allows goods to enter a country temporarily without the importer having to pay customs duties at the time of import, subject to compliance with the applicable conditions.Often described as a passport for goods, the document simplifies customs procedures for businesses and individuals transporting professional equipment, commercial samples and exhibition materials across international borders.The system is particularly useful for companies participating in overseas trade fairs, exhibitions and business events. It also helps media organisations and professionals who need to carry specialised equipment across countries for temporary assignments.However, the duty-free facility comes with an important condition: the goods must be re-exported within the permitted period.

items.title: Outlook outage scam: Beware of fake refund emails
Outlook down? Don't reset your password yet
items.summary: Microsoft outage today: Outlook users not able to access emails during the Microsoft 365 outage should resist the urge to reset their passwords/ reinstall Office. These fixes may seem worth trying when an inbox suddenly stops working but they won't help as Microsoft's services are down.MQTec Managing Director Moneeb Qureshi has warned users against making unnecessary changes to their Outlook accounts and software while Microsoft works to address the disruption.Microsoft outage began on Thursday affecting "Exchange Online". Outlook users experienced problems accessing their mailboxes through desktop, web and mobile applications, while email delivery was delayed.Outlook Not Working: Experts Say Leave Your Account Settings AloneA sudden Outlook error doesn't mean something is wrong with your password or computer. During a wider Microsoft 365 outage, the problem is beyond a user's control.Qureshi advised against resetting passwords, rebuilding Outlook profiles or changing DNS, proxy and sign-in settings without a specific reason. Unnecessary changes could leave users with additional configuration problems even after Microsoft restores its services.Checking Microsoft's public service status page is a better first step. Administrators can also look at the Service health section of the Microsoft 365 admin centre for updates.135804339Microsoft 365 Problems Extend to Teams and SharePointThe outage has affected more than email. While Teams chats, calls & meetings remained available. But calendar functions, scheduling & invitations faced problems.SharePoint users could still access files, although external file sharing was affected. Copilot, To Do & Planner also experienced unreliable loading. Some Defender and Purview security features operated with limitations.Microsoft's initial investigation found that an unexpectedly large number of servers had become unavailable and increased pressure on the remaining infrastructure. Microsoft said there was no indication of an attack.Are Outlook Emails Being Lost During the Microsoft OutageDelayed emails are not necessarily lost. And email systems generally try to deliver messages again when the receiving server becomes available.As per MQTec, Microsoft extended Exchange Online's normal 24 hour delivery window to 48 hours during the disruption, allowing delayed messages more time to reach recipients.Qureshi advised users not to resend emails. But they should do so only after receiving a non-delivery report confirming that the original message failed.135802371How to Keep Business Communications Running As Microsoft Is DownMQTec recommends that businesses have backup communication arrangements rather than relying entirely on Outlook.Emergency email accounts with another provider can help essential employees stay in touch during an outage. Businesses can also consider email continuity services that retain incoming messages until Microsoft 365 becomes available again.Locally stored data is another option. Outlook cached mode allows users to access previously downloaded emails, calendars and contacts without a server connection. OneDrive files may also remain accessible when they have been synchronised and configured to stay on the device.135781761

Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) on Friday sought to dispel concerns over the ethanol content of E20 petrol, saying a photograph circulating on social media from a fuel-quality demonstration in Karnataka was captured before the testing process had been completed and did not represent the final test result.
Clarifying the controversy, the state-owned oil marketing company in a statement said the image showed an intermediate stage of an ethanol separation test, in which the mixture of petrol and water initially turns hazy or milky before the two layers separate completely.
The photograph was inadvertently shared before the separation process was complete, following which the officer concerned promptly removed the post to prevent misinterpretation, BPCL said. The sample tested was found to be within prescribed specifications, it added.

items.summary: Fintech major Razorpay Software Ltd has moved a step closer to its stock market debut after receiving approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its initial public offering (IPO), according to an update on the regulator's website.The market regulator issued its final observations on Razorpay's draft offer documents on November 3, clearing the way for the company to proceed with the next stages of its listing process. Renewable energy independent power producer Sembcorp Green Infra also received Sebi's approval, on November 13, the update showed.Razorpay had confidentially filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with Sebi in June. The confidential filing route allows companies to obtain regulatory feedback without immediately making their financial statements and other sensitive business information public.The Bengaluru-based company is working towards a listing in the first quarter of 2027, ET had reported earlier this month. However, the timeline could be pushed back depending on market conditions and investor appetite. The final IPO launch date and pricing will be determined by demand from institutional and retail investors, as well as broader equity market sentiment.ET had reported on April 20 that Razorpay was preparing a confidential IPO filing to raise Rs 5,500-6,500 crore at an expected valuation of around $5 billion, or Rs 49,000-50,000 crore. This would be below the $7.5 billion valuation the company commanded in its last major private funding round in 2021.Subsequently, the fintech has also attracted investor interest at a lower valuation of around $3 billion, or Rs 30,000 crore, reflecting the more cautious approach investors have adopted towards valuations of technology companies ahead of their public listings.Razorpay's shareholders have approved a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,700 crore, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) through which existing investors can partially pare their holdings. Axis Capital, JPMorgan, Citi and Kotak Mahindra Capital are advising the company on the proposed IPO.The Sebi approval comes at a time when public market investors are increasingly scrutinising the growth, profitability and valuations of India's new-age technology companies. Walmart-backed payments rival PhonePe had paused its IPO plans earlier this year amid market uncertainty, highlighting the importance of timing for fintech companies looking to tap public markets.ALSO READ: Razorpay gets Sebi nod for Rs 5,000-6,000 crore IPO: sourcesFounded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay provides businesses with online and offline payment acceptance solutions, cross-border payments and a range of financial services. Its investors include Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Y Combinator and GIC.The company reported a 65% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 3,783 crore in FY25, compared with Rs 2,296 crore in the previous financial year. However, it posted a consolidated net loss of Rs 1,209 crore, largely due to expenses related to employee stock options, restructuring and tax costs associated with shifting its domicile to India."FY25 was a pivotal year for Razorpay. We delivered top-line growth through strong execution, while simultaneously improving our gross margins," cofounder and chief executive Harshil Mathur had said while announcing the company's financial results.Ahead of its proposed listing, Razorpay has also recalibrated its offline payments business, shifting its focus towards merchants that require an integrated online and offline payments offering. The move is aimed at improving operating efficiency and profitability as the company prepares to face public market scrutiny.The company completed its reverse flip, moving its domicile from the US to India in May 2025, removing a key structural hurdle ahead of a domestic listing.More recently, it received a final payment service provider licence to operate from Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City). The licence is expected to expand its ability to facilitate foreign-currency transactions and cross-border fund flows.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. PM Modi and Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar together flagged off the new services and travelled on the Metro train. Modi and Shivakumar were also seen buying separate tickets from the counter.

Governor Sudha Yadav, MP Tejasvi Surya and Minister K B Gowda also travelled in the Metro train.
The total length of the Pink Line is 21.25 km, comprising 18 stations. While the elevated corridor, which the prime minister inaugurated, has six stations, the underground section will have 12 stations and is still under construction.

items.title: Supply shocks to weaken monetary policy effectiveness: CEA Nageswaran
items.summary:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran on Friday said monetary policy tools such as interest rate adjustments may become less effective in tackling inflation in a world increasingly vulnerable to supply-side disruptions.
"Fiscal and other public policy measures will be more important because raising interest rates will not solve the supply-induced problems. If anything, it may even be counter-productive," he said at the 9th Annual Food Systems Dialogue here.
Amid persistent supply induced issues, countries will have to use all kinds of flexibilities with regards to the inflation targeting framework, he said.
"Since 2022, very few countries have met their inflation target. So, it will be there as a framework, but I think countries will take creative liberties with it, as they have to," he added.

items.title: Manappuram Finance shares drop 3% even as Q2 net profit soars 3x to Rs 701 crore. Why did Jefferies cut target price?
items.summary: Shares of Manappuram Finance dropped around 3% on Friday after the company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 701 crore for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027, surging over 3 times from Rs 220 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.The gold loan provider’s revenue from operations jumped 48% year-on-year to Rs 3,362 crore during the quarter under review, from Rs 2,274 crore reported in the same period last year. The company’s total expenses jumped more than 23% YoY to Rs 2,434 crore, from Rs 1,973 crore reported in the year-ago period. Manappuram Finance’s gold loan and other segment recorded around 54% YoY rise in revenue to Rs 3,043 crore, while that for micro finance rose over 12% YoY to Rs 329 crore. The company’s standalone assets under management expanded 69% year-on-year to Rs 63733 crore at the end of September. The shares of the company dropped to Rs 311 apiece on NSE on Friday morning.Also read | Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit soars 77% YoY, but NPAs riseJefferies on Manappuram Finance share priceJefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Manappuram Finance shares but reduced its target price to Rs 400 apiece from Rs 430. The latest target price implies 25% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 320 apiece on NSE.The international brokerage noted that the company’s Q2 profit was 5% ahead of its estimates as higher net interest income offset higher provisions. It expects branch expansion and customer growth to drive 23% gold loan growth and 18% consolidated AUM growth in FY27. The company’s NIM rose 63 basis points sequentially to 11%, while gold loan yields rose 30 basis points QoQ to 18%, likely driven by customers slipping into higher-yielding (lower-rebate) slabs with longer repayment cycles, as per the rebate pricing structure, as well as penalty charges. Mannapuram Finance plans to price its loans competitively, but expects gold loan yields to sustain at 17.5-18%.However, the company saw some stress in shorter tenure schemes like peers. Its management indicated incremental trends are better as customers adapt, although the company is gradually shifting to longer tenure schemes.Also read | Manappuram Finance's Stage 2 gold loans jump tenfold to 5%Jefferies raised FY27-28 EPS estimates by 3-4%, factoring in lower AUM growth, better NIMs, lower opex & higher credit costs. It highlighted that the spot gold price is down 7% since September and may remain range-bound over the near term amid Fed rate hikes. “We expect profit to rise 3x (off weak FY26 base) with ROE improving to 14% (7% FY26) over FY26-28. At 1.4x FY28 BV, valuations seem reasonable,” the international brokerage said.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Sensex, Nifty's explosive rally pushes market to pre-Middle East war levels. How long will they take to scale fresh peaks?
items.summary: The return of FIIs and easing oil prices sparked a skyrocketing rally in the Indian stock market this month, pushing the benchmark indices to levels not seen since the Middle East war ensued earlier this year, but analysts say it may take a few more months for them to hit fresh lifetime highs.Sensex this week touched 82,000, marking the first time since last February before US-Israel’s joint air strikes killed Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, beginning a conflict that sparked a sharp surge in oil prices and spooked investors, continuing till date. Nifty traded above 25,350 before the infamous March selloff began. The index has now traced its way back above the level.Also read |Sensex erases all Middle East war losses but is it too soon to forget the Hormuz factor?How far are Sensex, Nifty from their lifetime highs?Despite the recent gains, the benchmark indices are sharply down from their respective lifetime lows. Sensex had hit a lifetime high of 86,159 on December 1 last year, and Nifty had hit an all-time high of 26,373 early in January this year. The benchmark indices are around 5% away from their respective record peaks despite the recent rally.Sensex has recovered over 11,000 from its recent low to hover near 81,900, which leaves 86,000 about 5% away. Vaqarjaved Khan, Senior Fundamental analyst at Angel One, feels that this rally has fundamental support. Earnings visibility is improving, banking, autos and consumption are showing healthier demand, and softer input costs are helping margins, he said, adding that steady SIP flows from domestic investors also give the market a cushion even when foreign money turns cautious. Sensex’s recovery of over 11,000 points from its October low reflects a sharp improvement in market sentiment, supported by renewed foreign institutional inflows, easing crude oil prices and encouraging corporate earnings, said Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research, Ventura. Why caution is warranted after such sharp spikeHowever, after such a steep rally, some consolidation and profit booking cannot be ruled out, the analyst said. While the broader market outlook remains positive, geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures and fluctuations in foreign capital flows could create intermittent volatility, according to Bolinjkar. “We expect the next leg of the rally to be increasingly driven by earnings growth rather than liquidity alone.”“I would not call valuations comfortable after such a sharp run. Earnings need to catch up with prices, and that is what I will be watching in the coming quarters. Crude oil, global cues and foreign inflows will decide how quickly we move,” Khan from Angel One said.The current rally has been driven by falling crude levels, the return of foreign money and better-than-expected earnings. All three need to hold, and none of them is guaranteed while the US-Iran situation remains unresolved and the Fed stays hawkish, said Tanvi Kanchan, Associate Director at Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers. She noted that the market is already showing signs of fatigue near these levels as the Sensex has slipped back from its November 11 high and has been trading in a narrow range on Thursday.Also read | Rs 80,000 crore FII buying sparks explosive rally on Dalal Street. Will RBI rate hike worries kill the party?When could Sensex, Nifty soar back to lifetime highs?A fresh lifetime high, which is sustainable, is a realistic possibility over the next few months rather than the next few sessions, provided crude stays contained and foreign flows remain positive, one can expect short term consolidation before the breakout, according to Kanchan from Anand Rathi.Khan from Angel One has a base case that the Sensex can cross 86,000 and set a fresh lifetime high in roughly three to six months, provided Q3 FY27 earnings hold up and there is no external shock. “I would advise investors not to chase the rally and to accumulate quality large caps on dips.”Ventura analyst Vinit Bolinjkar believes that Sensex could test the 86,000–86,200 zone over the next two to three months, provided foreign inflows remain strong, crude prices stay contained and corporate earnings sustain their momentum. “A decisive breakout above the immediate resistance of 82,500 could pave the way towards 84,000 and eventually 86,000,” he said.Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, said if the market succeeds in holding on to its bullish momentum, Sensex could potentially revisit its lifetime highs over the next 3-6 weeks. “However, investors should not expect the rally to be linear. After such a sharp recovery, intermittent profit-booking and consolidation would be healthy and could provide a stronger base for the next leg of the uptrend,” according to Shah.Ajit Mishra, SVP of Research at Religare Broking, meanwhile believe Sensex is well positioned to reclaim the 86,000 mark and potentially surpass its previous lifetime high over the next 3-6 months. However, the next leg of the rally will need earnings delivery rather than just valuation re-rating, he said, adding that investors should use intermittent corrections to accumulate fundamentally strong businesses with sustainable growth prospects.Also read |MSCI rejig: LIC, Meesho, Coforge set to gain from index inclusion. How much inflows could they attract?Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. The company said both were its highest-ever Q2 figures since its listing in March 2019.Also Read | Ola Electric shares sink 6% as Q2 revenue falls 39% YoY. What's next?Revenue from operations increased 29.4% to Rs 110.02 crore, while total income rose 36.1% to Rs 139.21 crore. Standalone profit before tax climbed 50.5% to Rs 99.54 crore, while standalone profit after tax increased 51.8% to Rs 74.61 crore.The earnings growth was supported by a sharp increase in e-commerce activity. MSTC facilitated the sale of residential and multipurpose land parcels in Hyderabad, valued at Rs 2,863 crore, on behalf of the Telangana State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation and the Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority.The company also partnered with the Karnataka Excise Department for the e-auction of liquor shop licences. The first tranche covered 125 licences and fetched around Rs 125 crore for the state government.Also Read | Jensen Huang forfeits $108 million in unvested Nvidia equityOther transactions during the quarter included the sale of an ONGC oil rig for $5.8 million, the first coal gasification event on behalf of the Ministry of Coal, and auctions of mineral and coal assets.MSTC also launched the eighth tranche of critical mineral block auctions, involving 13 new blocks and seven previously offered blocks. It sold around 400,000 tonnes of chrome valued at about Rs 718 crore and 1.54 million tonnes of coal valued at Rs 175 crore.The company’s e-commerce vertical remains its core growth driver. MSTC’s presentation showed that the platform crossed Rs 545.80 billion in transaction value during the first half of FY27, although the company has exited its legacy trading business.Another trigger for the stock was the RBI’s in-principle authorisation, received on November 11, to set up and operate a Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act. The board has directed the management to take the necessary steps to comply with the conditions attached to the approval.MSTC said it is developing the TReDS platform and is also examining the feasibility of setting up coal and other mineral exchanges. Its B2B travel portal is ready and is being upgraded for B2C operations.The Q2 performance marks a sharp improvement in profitability, with income growth significantly outpacing the rise in expenses. Consolidated expenses increased 9.8% YoY to Rs 39.67 crore in the quarter, compared with a 36.1% increase in total income.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. items.title: India must hold satellite 'kill switch', avoid reliance on one firm: Mittal
items.summary:
Bharti Airtel Founder and Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said India must keep control of the "kill switch" for satellite communications on its own soil, as the government weighs security conditions that will decide when satellite broadband goes live.
"The kill switch, as we call it, should not be sitting somewhere else," Mittal said in an interview with PTI marking Bharti Enterprises' 50th year. "India must have control over its own space destiny."
He did not name a company in that remark.
The kill switch is the ability to cut off, throttle or restrict a satellite network's service, whether for a single terminal, a region or an entire country, from the operator's control systems and ground gateways. items.title: Sairang Express derailment: Initial probe points to faulty braking system
items.summary:
A preliminary probe into the derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express at Digaru Railway Station in Assam on November 11 has pointed to a malfunctioning main braking system on the train.
A six-member probe team, in its report, found that the system primarily responsible for applying brakes in the coaches, technically known as the BP angle cock, was in an isolated condition in the locomotive.
"This may be the reason for this accident, as the brakes may not have been applied when the FP/BP angle cock of the loco was in an isolated condition," a joint note prepared by the probe team on the day of the accident said.
It further stated that the train crew applied the brakes, "but the brakes may not have been applied as the angle cock was previously in the closed position".
The probe report does not identify who rendered the braking system dysfunctional or whether the train crew overlooked safety procedures to check its functionality before operating the train.

items.title: US 'not sure' if Alice Huang was Chinese spy
items.summary: US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday that the Justice Department has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman who had an affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was a Chinese spy.Blanche said at a press conference that "of course" the FBI was investigating reports that Alice Huang was working for the Chinese government.Also read: US probes alleged spy Alice Huang over suspected Super Micro chip smuggling to China: ReportUS President Donald Trump, asked in an interview released later on Thursday whether Huang should have resigned, reiterated that it was not yet determined whether Alice Huang was a spy."The big thing is, was the woman a spy? And I don't know if that's been determined yet. But if the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different," Trump told the "Straight Shooter" podcast, adding that he spoke to Jensen Huang on Wednesday.Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday in a departure that unfolded over more than a year, beginning with an October 2025 New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, an official Nvidia cloud partner, a coveted status that gave it priority access to Nvidia chips.Also read: Nvidia faced pressure to boost its AI backstop before Jensen Huang's exitSubsequent reports said US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. DIIs book profits in longest selling streak in 4 years
items.summary: Mumbai: Their roles have decidedly reversed.For years, domestic funds have provided the backstop against exiting foreigners, lifting the share of local stock ownership to a record and preventing a rout of Indian risk assetsOver the past fortnight, however, as foreign funds have come flooding in, domestic institutional investors (DII) have sought to book the profit of patience.Mutual funds, banks, insurers and retirement funds have turned net sellers over the past nine sessions, marking their longest selling streak in four years.135785472Their exits coincide with the sharpest rally in Indian benchmark indices in years - and the meltdown of AI-themed trades in eastern Asia.Data from the NSE showed that DIIs sold equities worth over ₹47,662 crore between October 30 and November 12, marking their longest selling streak since November 2022 when DIIs sold for 10 straight sessions.Read more: New SIP registrations fall 20%, stoppage ratio climbs to 116% in October after 5-month decline If the trend continues, November could become the first month of net selling by DIIs since July 2023, when they offloaded around ₹2,700 crore. It could also mark their steepest monthly selling since November 2020, when they sold equities worth around ₹48,000 crore.Read more: Meesho block deal: SoftBank-backed entity likely to sell 1% stake worth Rs 1,174 croreNilesh Shah, managing director, Kotak Mahindra AMC, said the bulk of the selling is likely coming from profit-booking and portfolio rebalancing by Multi-Asset Allocation Funds (MAFs), Balanced Advantage Funds (BAFs), insurance companies and pension funds. The market rally has pushed up their equity exposure, prompting them to book profits to maintain their targeted asset allocation. Arbitrage funds have also contributed to the selling, albeit to a smaller extent, by exploiting reverse arbitrage opportunities in mid-cap stocks, where futures are trading at a discount to the cash market, prompting funds to sell shares and buy futures, Shah added.The DII selling comes even as foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have returned to Indian equities. Since the beginning of November, the Sensex and Nifty have gained nearly 10% each, while the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices have advanced around 8% each. FPIs have invested around $8 billion in Indian equities since mid-October, amid a correction in AI-related stocks globally and a decline in crude oil prices.Despite the recent selling, DIIs have remained a key source of support for the market through the year. Akshat Garg, AVP - Research & Product at Choice Wealth, said DIIs had been net buyers of over ₹6.5 lakh crore in 2026, supported by steady SIP and insurance inflows through market corrections. Following the sharp recovery, they are now trimming exposure to richly valued pockets, raising cash and allowing returning foreign investors to take on the role of marginal buyers.

items.title: US stocks: US market closes lower as Nvidia slide outweighs energy rally
items.summary: US stocks closed lower on Thursday, as a drop in Nvidia shares after CEO Jensen Huang's exit outweighed gains in energy shares.The chip company's shares fell but were well off the day's lowest level after earlier dropping nearly 12%. Retail investors bought Nvidia shares worth about $111 million in the first half hour of trading, the biggest opening bid on record for the stock, according to data from Vanda Analytics.The S&P 500 lost 25.99 points, or 0.34%, to end at 7,593.39 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 102.44 points, or 0.40%, to 25,363.75. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 190.29 points, or 0.36%, to 52,296.20. The S&P 500 energy index gained about 2%, making it the best performer among the benchmark’s 11 major sectors. Crude prices rose after President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US did not need a deal with Iran.AI-linked stocks fell globally after Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. AI cloud company Nebius tumbled nearly 18% following its quarterly results and outlook.However, Nvidia rivals and other major technology companies, including Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet and Amazon, advanced and provided the biggest support to the S&P 500.Stocks have been volatile in recent days as sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections fueled concerns about tighter AI regulation. Uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership has also pressured one of the main drivers of the current bull market.Also Read | US stocks: Nvidia shares plunge 13% after Jensen Huang quits as CEO; Colette Kress named interim chief“Right now, the market is selling AI stocks and tech stocks and buying safe stuff, just like it did in the first halo trade in January and February of this year, but it will flip back,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis.“That’s the tug of war the market is doing right now. It’s concerns about deceleration versus just pointing out that the absolute valuation and growth rates are still pretty compelling.”Nvidia’s financing ties face scrutinyHuang’s departure is expected to intensify scrutiny of AI companies with close financial ties to Nvidia.The chipmaker has backed several businesses, including some of its customers, through financing arrangements that investors are reassessing following the leadership change.Also Read | Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit raises fears over the future of AI financing“Nvidia is the circular-funder-in-chief; they’re the biggest by far at this point, and I assume that activity will moderate,” Ellerbroek said.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 0.5% after gaining 17.2% over the previous four sessions. CoreWeave dropped about 7%, while shares of data-center companies IREN and Applied Digital also declined.Investors await inflation dataInvestors are looking to Friday’s Producer Price Index for further indications about inflation after consumer prices rose more than expected earlier in the week.Markets are fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate increase of at least 25 basis points in December, with a 15% probability of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Comments from several Fed officials this week suggested the central bank could consider a more aggressive path of rate increases as price pressures intensify.Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Thursday that she did not believe the central bank needed to shift to larger rate increases to control inflation. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said rates would probably need to rise further to address elevated inflation but did not indicate any urgency.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit raises fears over the future of AI financing
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday raised concerns not only about the future of the multitrillion-dollar chipmaker but also about its willingness and ability to continue financing the artificial intelligence boom, Reuters reported.Huang’s exit added another pressure point to one of the global market’s most crowded trades. It came after Nvidia’s board met late Wednesday to consider the longtime CEO’s future following reports of two extramarital affairs.Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor, the company said in a statement.Investors initially sold Nvidia shares and stocks linked to the company, including data-centre operator CoreWeave and South Korea’s Naver. Shares of chipmaking rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices advanced.Chinese graphics-processing-unit makers also rallied on expectations that Nvidia’s leadership upheaval could help local suppliers gain market share. Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each surged nearly 10%.Nvidia shares fell 13%, while Nasdaq 100 futures declined 0.6%.The broader concern is that Nvidia could scale back its strategy of financing data centres under new leadership, potentially slowing investment across the AI industry.Also Read | Anthropic IPO: Can Indian investors apply for Claude maker's $64 billion share sale? Check rules“Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. They’ll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, according to Reuters.Nvidia has been the flagship stock of the AI revolution. Its technological lead and surging sales have driven its share price up about 900% in the four years since the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT helped usher in the generative-AI era.The company has also emerged as a major financier of the industry, investing billions of dollars in customers through equity stakes and other financial commitments as it anticipates growing demand for increasingly powerful chips.“Nvidia’s credit support is what makes much of this debt finance-able across the AI hyperscaler deal front,” said Christopher Brown, senior vice president, investments, at Synovus Securities. “Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.”Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into Huang after reports that he had an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. A separate report involving another alleged affair emerged before Wednesday’s board meeting.Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters that Nvidia’s revenue was unlikely to fall suddenly following Huang’s departure. The greater concern, he said, was the company’s long-term direction because of Huang’s central role in shaping its computing strategy.“Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge,” Boloor said.Nvidia’s departure reverberates across AI stocksHuang’s exit creates a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4 trillion company he co-founded and built over more than three decades. Nvidia has become the leading supplier of AI chips and a focal point of the technology rivalry between the United States and China.Asian chip stocks, which had rallied alongside Nvidia during the AI spending boom but recently came under pressure from concerns about financing costs and demand, also declined.Nvidia disclosed $164.5 billion in financial commitments in its latest earnings report. These included an obligation of up to $105 billion tied to an OpenAI data centre in Ohio and more than $50 billion in lease and capacity guarantees.In August, Nvidia said it had partnered with six major financial institutions, including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone, to establish computing-finance platforms seeking more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Huang said the company could backstop as much as $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals.“The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raise the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility,” Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters.Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot. Anthropic’s initial public offering this month is expected to test investor demand for AI-related assets.CoreWeave shares fell more than 7.5% in premarket trading after surging Wednesday on upbeat earnings. Naver, in which Nvidia invested $1 billion by financing a data-centre expansion, dropped 6%.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit jumps over 3-fold to ₹701 crore
items.summary:
Gold loan financier Manappuram Finance Ltd on Thursday reported a more than three-fold year-on-year increase in its consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 701 crore for the September quarter of FY27.
The company had posted a PAT of Rs 217.31 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. On a sequential basis, net profit rose 20 per cent from Rs 585 crore in the June quarter.
Total income increased to Rs 3,312 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 2,275 crore in the year-ago period, the company said in a regulatory filing.
The company's total assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 73,303 crore as of September 2026, registering a year-on-year growth of 60 per cent.
Gold Loan AUM surged 92.5 per cent YoY to Rs 60,640 crore at the end of the September quarter.
Shares of Manappuram Finance settled 0.23 per cent lower at Rs 320.25 apiece on the BSE.

items.title: What Nvidia said after CEO’s shocking exit
items.summary: In a move that would certainly send shockwaves through the tech world, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company as president, chief executive officer (CEO) and a member of the company's board of directors, with immediate effect on Thursday.Meanwhile, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been appointed as interim chief executive officer as the chip giant begins a search for a permanent successor.Nvidia's board said it will consider both internal and external candidates for the position. Kress will continue to serve as the company's executive vice president and CFO while serving as interim CEO until a permanent successor is appointed.Also Read | Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO amid affair scandal; AI chip giant names Colette Kress interim chiefThe company did not disclose a reason for Huang's resignation in its announcement.Kress has served as Nvidia's executive vice president and CFO since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company's finance organisation and played a key role in Nvidia's growth and evolution.Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.What Nvidia's board saidHarvey C. Jones, who has been appointed Nvidia's first-ever chair of the board, said Kress has helped lead the company through a period of “extraordinary growth” and has a deep understanding of its business, customers, operations and financial position.The board said it has “full confidence” in Kress and the leadership team and expects Nvidia's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said.She added that Nvidia would continue advancing its work in accelerated computing and AI while focusing on customers, partners, developers and shareholders.Also Read | Jensen Huang and the Chinese spy honeytrap: How does China allegedly use this strategy to gather sensitive US information?Jensen Huang's Nvidia legacyThe board said Huang's contributions to Nvidia were “profound” and described the company as one of the world's most consequential technology companies.“The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said.Huang founded Nvidia and has led the company for 33 years, overseeing its transformation into a dominant player in accelerated computing and AI.A private affair, a very public exitHuang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been at the helm of the company for more than three decades. During that time, he transformed Nvidia from a graphics chipmaker into one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global artificial intelligence boom. His departure marks a major change for the company and the semiconductor industry.Huang's exit comes amid a controversy involving Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, whom US intelligence agencies suspect of gathering information for Beijing. Huang admitted to having an extramarital relationship with her and apologised to his wife, children and Nvidia employees.The revelations prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company, however, said its board had no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's confidential information had been compromised. The affair finally cost Huang to step down from his position from the company.

items.title: Kimberly Powell: Nvidia career in spotlight
items.summary: Kimberly Powell has spent 18 years at Nvidia, moving from medical imaging to some of the company's biggest healthcare AI projects, including genomics and drug discovery. But the 48-year-old vice president is now in the headlines for a different reason.The New York Times reported on November 11 that she had an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, 63, who is her direct boss. The report cited five people who worked at the company and said the two were seen being affectionate in a video recorded at a San Jose hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. Powell is married, the newspaper reported.When the Times asked Huang about his relationship with Powell, he reportedly replied, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before ending the call. Powell and Nvidia had not responded to Business Insider's requests for comment as of November 12. Neither has confirmed the reported relationship.The report comes as Nvidia is already dealing with another controversy involving Huang. The CEO recently told employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming anyone.Separately, the company's board has been examining whether a technology executive with alleged links to Chinese intelligence targeted Huang. That case involves Alice Huang, not Kimberly Powell. Together, the developments have put the company's leadership, internal policies and board oversight under fresh scrutiny.Who is Kimberly Powell and what is her role at Nvidia?Powell is one of Nvidia's senior executives responsible for taking its AI computing technology beyond conventional chip applications. Her current role covers healthcare and life sciences, two areas where Nvidia wants to expand the use of accelerated computing and artificial intelligence.        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Yahoo Finance (@yahoofinance)She joined Nvidia in 2008 as a director. Her initial responsibility was to establish Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) as computing accelerators for medical imaging equipment.Before joining Nvidia, Powell worked in hardware engineering and product management at Planar Systems, where she focused on diagnostic imaging systems. She holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, with a concentration in computer engineering, from Northeastern University.Her entry into Nvidia was not the result of a conventional executive recruitment process. On an August 2026 episode of the Lifers podcast, she explained that she had contacted Nvidia to discuss its computing technology. The company subsequently recognised its potential applications in healthcare and approached her about joining.She described the opportunity as a "dream come true."Powell's responsibilities grew over the years. Her LinkedIn profile says she became a senior director in 2016, leading an AI-focused business development team. In 2017, she was promoted to vice president of healthcare.When she joined in 2008, one of the main opportunities was using GPUs to process medical images. Medical imaging systems generate large volumes of data, and GPUs can process many calculations simultaneously. This makes them useful for applications such as analysing CT scans, MRI images and other diagnostic images.Over time, Nvidia expanded this approach into other parts of healthcare.Its medical imaging platform, MONAI, provides tools for developing AI applications that analyse medical images. Its BioNeMo platform supports AI research in biology and drug discovery. Parabricks uses accelerated computing to process genomic data.Powell's role has therefore expanded from promoting GPUs for imaging equipment to developing a wider computing and software ecosystem for healthcare companies, hospitals and pharmaceutical researchers.According to her profile on the Milken Institute's website, she also oversees the global strategy and commercial expansion of these platforms.Kimberly Powell report and Alice Huang investigationThe Powell report is the second major development involving Huang's personal relationships to emerge during Nvidia's current leadership crisis. But the two cases concern different women and different allegations.The first involves Alice Huang, a technology executive associated with Megaspeed. The New York Times previously reported that US officials believed she might have been recruited by the Chinese government to gather information about Nvidia.The allegations have raised national security questions because Nvidia makes some of the world's most advanced AI chips, which are subject to US export restrictions on sales to China.Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company has also faced scrutiny over its relationship with Alice Huang and the circumstances surrounding the alleged intelligence operation.The issue has also reached Congress. Republican lawmakers have sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on his relationship with Alice Huang and the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia's business in China.On November 11, Reuters reported that Nvidia's board had met to consider whether Huang should be removed as CEO. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that the board was preparing to oust him.Nvidia has 11 board members, including Huang. Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can remove him, with or without cause. All directors other than Huang are considered independent.As of November 12, no final removal decision had been publicly announced.Reuters also reported that there was no obvious successor if Huang were removed. Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress and senior data-centre executive Ian Buck have been mentioned in discussions about possible leadership arrangements, but no successor has been announced.Nvidia is scheduled to report its quarterly results on November 17.Nvidia shares closed at $173.73 on November 11, gaining 2.87% during the regular session. However, the stock fell more than 8% in extended trading after reports that the board was considering Huang's future.Reuters reported that Nvidia shares also fell around 7% in early Frankfurt trading on November 12. The company's market value had declined by roughly $600 billion since the board announced its investigation into the Alice Huang matter, according to the report.

Andhra urges Walmart to source from MSMEs
items.summary: On Thursday, Andhra Pradesh called on American retail major Walmart to expand its local procurement by bringing the state's MSMEs, women-led self-help groups (SHGs), and artisans into its supply network.The request was made during discussions between Andhra Pradesh's IT and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh and Paul Dyck, Walmart's Senior Vice President for Global Government Affairs and Business Diplomacy, who met on the sidelines of the 31st CII Partnership Summit."Andhra Pradesh is asking Walmart and Flipkart to widen their sourcing from the State beyond seafood and pharmaceuticals, to include its MSMEs, women-led self-help groups and artisans," an official statement noted.To build on the momentum of the New Delhi Walmart Growth Summit—which linked Indian vendors with the retailer's international buying teams, Lokesh proposed that Walmart host a specialized MSME sourcing event in Andhra Pradesh centered on seafood and textiles. He further recommended establishing a dedicated pipeline within Walmart and Flipkart’s domestic and international supply chains for goods produced by local artisans and women-led SHGs, specifically those marketed under the state's Swayam AP and Lepakshi labels.According to the official release, Dyck acknowledged that Walmart ranks among the top purchasers of Andhra Pradesh shrimp, buying over 65 million pounds annually, while also procuring textiles, engineering goods, and pharmaceuticals from the region.Furthermore, Flipkart's regional footprint has generated over 28,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities. Its operational infrastructure includes over 100 logistics hubs covering roughly 12 lakh sq ft, alongside 0.33 million sq ft dedicated to wholesale operations. Through a memorandum of understanding with the AP MSME Corporation and the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (RTIH), over 3,200 MSMEs have received training, resulting in more than 900 businesses actively selling on the Walmart and Flipkart platforms.Dyck assured that Walmart would review the state's recommendations."Walmart is already one of the largest buyers of Andhra Pradesh shrimp. Now we want them to look at the rest of what our State makes. Our MSMEs, women's groups and artisans make products of global quality. What they need is a direct line to global buyers, and Walmart and Flipkart can provide it," said Lokesh.

items.title: India’s Russian fossil fuel imports hit record
items.summary: India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October, purchasing hydrocarbons worth €6.4 billion, according to a monthly analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). It was India’s highest monthly total in data going back to January 2022.Crude oil accounted for 91% of India’s purchases at €5.8 billion. Coal imports were worth €333 million, while oil products accounted for €232 million.Indian refineries raise Russian crude purchasesIndia’s imports of Russian crude oil rose 10% from September. Imports increased at all three of the country’s largest importing refineries—Vadinar, Jamnagar and Paradip.Imports at Vadinar rose 12% month-on-month, while Jamnagar and Paradip recorded increases of 22% and 28%, respectively. The rise made Jamnagar the biggest importer of seaborne Russian crude in October.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei that use Russian crude exported oil products worth €1.6 billion to countries imposing sanctions in October. The destinations included the European Union, Australia, the US and New Zealand.Ten of the 12 shipments of oil products from refineries processing Russian crude that reached EU ports in October departed from India’s Jamnagar refinery. The remaining two shipments came from Turkiye’s STAR refinery.CREA estimated that €389 million worth of the oil products exported by these refineries were made from Russian crude. Exports from the refineries to sanctioning countries rose 21% in volume terms from September.Russia’s fossil fuel earnings reach four-year highChina remained the largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels, purchasing €10.7 billion worth of hydrocarbons in October. The European Union was the third-largest buyer at €2.2 billion, followed by Turkiye at €1.1 billion and South Korea at €488 million.Russia’s total fossil fuel export revenues rose 14% month-on-month to €754 million per day in October, the highest monthly level since December 2022. Export volumes remained broadly unchanged.Crude oil export revenues rose 19% to €449 million per day, with seaborne crude earnings increasing 23% to €352 million per day. CREA said this was the highest monthly level recorded since its data series began in January 2022.The report said higher global oil prices, linked to the energy crisis around the Strait of Hormuz, helped increase Russia’s fossil fuel earnings. Russia’s Urals crude averaged $101.70 a barrel in October, more than twice the EU and UK price cap of $44.10 a barrel.CREA also said that 60% of Russia’s seaborne oil was transported by sanctioned “shadow” tankers in October. Another 37% was carried by tankers owned or insured in G7 countries and their partners.A crude oil price cap of $30 a barrel, if fully enforced, would have reduced Russia’s seaborne crude oil export revenues by 21%, or €2.2 billion, in October, CREA said. A lower cap on crude and oil products together could have reduced Russia’s total seaborne oil export revenues by 25%, or €3.4 billion.

items.title: US stock market selloff: Four indicators suggest correction may not be over
items.summary: The recent selloff in US stocks has left investors searching for signs of a market bottom, but four key indicators suggest it may be too early to declare the correction over, according to a Reuters analysis.Technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks have fallen around 10% from their recent peaks after the Nasdaq-100 hit a record high in early October. While shares have stabilised somewhat, investor positioning, options activity and technical indicators continue to signal caution.Read more: Chinese yuan edges higher, but stronger dollar caps gains Technology positioning shows signs of easingAccording to Deutsche Bank data cited by Reuters, investors have reduced exposure to technology stocks since late September, shifting towards other sectors. The latest selloff pushed tech positioning below levels recorded during the April 2025 tariff-related market turmoil.Deutsche Bank strategist Parag Thatte said the decline appeared to be driven by investors unwinding crowded positions. He added that positioning levels could create conditions for a technology sector rebound.Stock correlations offer some reliefAnother relatively positive signal is the limited increase in expected stock correlations. Barclays strategists noted that three-month realised correlation among the 50 largest S&P 500 companies fell to a record low in late September.Although expectations for correlations increased during last week's selloff, the rise remained modest. Rocky Fishman, founder of Asym Research, said this suggested investors viewed the decline as a sector-specific correction rather than a broader economic downturn, Reuters reported.Read more: South Korean shares rise as tech stocks rebound on Wall StreetOptions activity presents a mixed pictureRetail investors had purchased call options on individual stocks in record volumes this year, helping support the AI rally. However, that trend reversed sharply last week.According to Carrick Lane data, retail call buying in AI stocks dropped significantly, contributing to the post-election selloff.The shift has reduced excessive bullish positioning, but options indicators have not weakened enough to provide a strong buying signal.Technical indicators remain cautiousTechnical signals continue to suggest that the market may not have reached its bottom. Mark Newton, head of technical strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors, said the rebound in the Invesco QQQ ETF, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, had stalled below its downward trend line.Weak short-term momentum and the absence of a DeMark exhaustion signal suggest US stocks could remain volatile for another couple of weeks, Newton said.Overall, while reduced technology exposure and relatively stable stock correlations offer some encouragement, options positioning and technical trends suggest investors should remain cautious before calling an end to the market correction.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times.)

Notably, this is only the second time in a month the stock has crossed this level. The sharp 9% surge over the two days has added more than Rs 1,400 crore to the company’s market capitalisation, pushing it above Rs 17,150 crore.Also read | EV makers turn to family scooters to drive mass-market adoptionAll about the centre’s new EV procurement policyThe Finance Ministry has made electric vehicles (EVs) the "default and preferred choice" for the procurement of government staff cars in all ministries and departments of the Centre, with immediate effect. It also doubled the net dealer price ceiling for the procurement of EVs by central government ministries and departments to Rs 20 lakh, while that for ICE vehicles, including petrol, diesel and hybrid cars, has been fixed at Rs 10 lakh.The government also mandated preference to EVs in hiring cars for government use. The moves are aimed to promote electric mobility, reducing dependence on fossil fuels, and taking into account the prevailing market prices and lifecycle costs of vehicles."Going forward, Ministries and Departments shall ordinarily procure Electric Vehicles (EVs) at the time of condemnation or replacement of their existing ICE staff cars. items.title: Oil below $92 amid hopes of peace talks
items.summary: Oil prices edged lower by more than $1 on Thursday as investors increasingly hopes for peace talks to resolve the Middle East conflict as well as the much-longer lasting Russia-Ukraine war.Brent crude futures fell more than $1 to trade below $92 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also lost over $1 to trade below $86 per barrel on Thursday morning. This comes after Brent crude rose over 1% on Wednesday after hitting two-month lows in the previous day.Russian and Ukrainian negotiators have agreed to a major prisoner exchange during their peace talks held over two days in Abu Dhabi, although US mediators said differences remained on other major issues, including territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country hoped to achieve concrete results on resolving the war this year.Also read | India's battered rupee finds an unlikely rescue party in cheaper oil and Wall Street's AI routBack in the Middle East, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the government will not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave Iran and there will be consequences if the US launches new strikes. The US meanwhile has said that nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the eight-month-old war, while US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes.Meanwhile, OPEC+ crude oil production jumped in October, driven by a sharp increase in output from Saudi Arabia despite continued disruption to shipments through the Hormuz Strait. US crude stocks jumped by 9 million barrels in the latest week, Reuters quoted market sources as saying, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.Where are oil prices heading for?While oil prices have dropped from their multi decade highs which they hit earlier this year, analysts remain cautious amid the seesaw political game in the Middle East. Goldman Sachs recently raised its oil price forecasts, citing increasing risks to global supplies. The investment bank warned that Brent crude could climb to $140 per barrel in 2027 if oil production across the Gulf region remains significantly below its 2025 average.Goldman Sachs recently raised its oil price forecasts, citing increasing risks to global supplies. The investment bank warned that Brent crude could climb to $140 per barrel in 2027 if oil production across the Gulf region remains significantly below its 2025 average.Also read | India in a 'sweet spot' amid oil volatility and currency dynamics: Kotak Neo's Anindya BanerjeeIn an upside scenario, Brent crude could reach $140 per barrel and average around $130 in 2027 if Gulf oil production remains 3.5 million barrels per day below its 2025 average, Reuters reported, citing Goldman Sachs' projections.Goldman Sachs expects oil markets to incorporate a higher geopolitical risk premium, given the possibility of disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies, the historical duration of major supply shocks and the challenges involved in securing a lasting diplomatic breakthrough.JPMorgan analysts also highlighted the uncertainty surrounding the conflict, saying it remained difficult to predict how the war would unfold. At the outset, the bank had expected the US administration to avoid crossing certain economic thresholds. Indians buy 30% more gold after recent price correction
items.summary: Kolkata: Indians stepped up purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period despite elevated prices, with gold buying rising 30% by volume and silver demand increasing 10% over the same period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said this signalled a revival of demand ahead of the crucial wedding season.As per the industry body, consumers bought 52 tonnes of gold worth ₹72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at ₹5,400 crore during this year's Dhanteras-Diwali. The surge came after gold prices corrected from a peak of around ₹1.8 lakh to ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams, encouraging buyers to return to the market. Advance purchases for the wedding season, which begins in mid-November and continues until March, also contributed to the increase.135751520"Jewellers have made good business in this year's Dhanteras and Diwali," said IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta.There was a pent-up demand in the market, after many consumers had earlier halted purchases following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal not to buy gold, he said. "Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing ."The timing of the festivals also supported purchases, with Dhanteras falling on November 6 and Diwali on November 8, both at the beginning of the month when most salaried people receive their salaries and festive bonus."This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment," said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council. This fiscal year till September, gold sales by volume fell by almost 50% due to price and import duty increase, and PM Modi's call to avoid purchase of gold.Read more: Smallcap mutual fund inflows drop 29% MoM to Rs 6,407 crore in October. Should investors be cautious or continue investing?Gold has delivered substantial returns over the past few years, with prices rising from around ₹60,000 per 10 gm in 2023 to ₹80,000 in 2024, ₹1.15-1.20 lakh in 2025 and about ₹1.42 lakh this year during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Silver too has witnessed significant appreciation. An analysis of eight years of business performance by Bengaluru-based C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers shows that gold sales volumes during this festive season were the third highest in a decade, despite prices being around 10% higher than a year ago."The overall sentiment has remained unshaken, with consumers continuing to repose confidence in gold jewellery despite the unprecedented rise in prices over a 12-month period," said C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers director C Vinod Hayagriv.Read more: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on ThursdayNatural diamond also demonstrated resilience, recording their second-highest sales volume in eight years. The retailer reported a 250% rise in natural diamond sales on Dhanteras and a 47% rise during the Diwali season. This comes amid turbulence in the natural diamond industry due to global sanctions affecting Russian diamond supplies and growing competition from lab-grown alternatives. Lab-grown diamonds are emerging as an additional category rather than replacing natural diamonds.
